(لا يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ جَمِيعاً إِلَّا فِي قُرىً مُحَصَّنَةٍ أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ جُدُرٍ): لا is negating; يقاتلونكم is an imperfect verb, nominative, with its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; جميعا is a ḥāl, i.e. all together; إلا is a particle of restriction; في قرى is attached to يقاتلونكم, and the pronoun refers to the Jews; محصنة is an adjective of قرى; أو is a conjunction; من وراء is conjoined to في قرى; and جدر is the muḍāf ilayhi; it is the plural of جدار, and it has been read in the singular.
(بَأْسُهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ شَدِيدٌ تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعاً وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّى): the clause is resumptive, explaining their state, i.e. they are of the utmost strength and courage when fighting one another, but when they fight you they become weak and cowardly. بأسهم is a mubtadaʾ; بينهم is an adverb attached to شديد; شديد is the khabar; the clause تحسبهم is also resumptive; تحسبهم is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and جميعا the second mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial; قلوبهم is a mubtadaʾ and شتى its khabar, and the clause is circumstantial.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded shortly.
(كَمَثَلِ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ قَرِيباً ذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ): كمثل is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "مثلهم" (their likeness); الذين is the muḍāf ilayhi; من قبلهم is the ṣila of الذين; قريبا is an adverb attached to the omitted [notion of] being (istiqrār) to which من قبلهم is attached; you may also attach it to ذاقوا. Al-Zamakhsharī attached it to an implied muḍāf in the khabar, i.e. "like the existence of the likeness of the people of Badr, recently", i.e. the likeness of the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr, in the exile, humiliation and abasement that befell them, is like the likeness of the people of Mecca in what also befell them on the day of Badr of defeat, captivity and killing; and his view is not far-fetched. ذاقوا is a verb and its fāʿil, and وبال أمرهم is the object.
(وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; لهم is a fronted khabar; عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ; and عظيم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has أليم] is an adjective, i.e. in the Hereafter.
(كَمَثَلِ الشَّيْطانِ إِذْ قالَ لِلْإِنْسانِ اكْفُرْ): كمثل is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the likeness of the hypocrites in inciting the Jews to fight is like the likeness of Satan. إذا [Translator's note: so in the source, for إذ] is an adverb of past time attached to the [notion of] being to which the khabar is attached; you may also attach it to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from مثل الشيطان, as if it were an explanation of it. The clause قال is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; للإنسان is attached to قال; and the clause اكفر is the object of the saying.
(فَلَمَّا كَفَرَ قالَ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنْكَ): the fāʿ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so he disbelieved; then when he disbelieved". لما is temporal (ḥīniyya), or a linking [particle] containing the meaning of condition; the clause كفر is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; the clause قال has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; إنّ and its noun, and بريء is its predicate; and منك is attached to بريء.
(إِنِّي أَخافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ): the clause is a false justification of his disowning him, for otherwise he does not fear Allah. إنّ and its noun, and the clause أخاف الله is its predicate; and رب العالمين is a badal (substitute) of الله or an adjective of it.
(فَكانَ عاقِبَتَهُما أَنَّهُما فِي النَّارِ خالِدَيْنِ فِيها وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ): the fāʿ is conjunctive; كان is a defective past verb and عاقبتهما is its fronted predicate, i.e. [the end] of the misleader and the misled; أنّ and what lies in its scope is the khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; on the parsing just given it is the noun of كان]; أنّ and its noun, and في النار is its predicate; خالدين is a ḥāl; فيها is attached to خالدين; the wāw is resumptive; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the punishment; and جزاء الظالمين is the khabar of ذلك.

dervis-irab:18-24.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ): a resumptive statement brought to address the believers and give them admonition. اتقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and الله its object; the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; تنظر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; نفس is the fāʿil; ما is the object of تنظر; the clause قدّمت is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. قدّمته; and لغد is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قدّمت. "Tomorrow" was applied to the Day of Resurrection to represent it as near. Further discussion of the meaning of "tomorrow" will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): He repeated the command to fear [Him] for emphasis. The clause إن الله خبير بما تعملون is the reason for the command to fear [Him]; and إنّ with its noun and its predicate.
(وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَأَنْساهُمْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تكونوا is a defective imperfect verb, jussive by لا; the wāw is its noun and كالذين its predicate; the clause نسوا الله is the ṣila of the relative noun. فأنساهم: the fāʿ is conjunctive; أنساهم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أنفسهم is the second mafʿūl bihi.
(أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; and الفاسقون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, the clause then being the khabar of أولئك.
(لا يَسْتَوِي أَصْحابُ النَّارِ وَأَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ): لا is negating; يستوي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); أصحاب النار is the fāʿil; and أصحاب الجنة is conjoined to أصحاب النار.
(أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمُ الْفائِزُونَ): a resumptive statement brought to explain the manner of the inequality. أصحاب الجنة is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation or a second mubtadaʾ; and الفائزون is the khabar in either case. Its counterpart has preceded shortly.
(لَوْ أَنْزَلْنا هذَا الْقُرْآنَ عَلى جَبَلٍ لَرَأَيْتَهُ خاشِعاً مُتَصَدِّعاً مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement brought for comparison. لو is conditional; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; هذا is the mafʿūl bihi and القرآن a badal (substitute); على جبل is attached to أنزلنا; the lām links the answer of لو; رأيته is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; خاشعا is a second object or a ḥāl (circumstantial), since the seeing may be mental or visual; متصدعا is a second ḥāl or an adjective of خاشعا; and من خشية الله is attached to متصدعا.
(وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثالُ نَضْرِبُها لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; تلك is a mubtadaʾ; الأمثال is a badal; the clause نضربها is the khabar; للناس is attached to نضربها; لعلّ and its noun, and the clause يتفكرون is its predicate.
(هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ; الله is a first khabar; الذي is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause لا إله إلا هو is the ṣila. The i'rab of the word of testimony (kalimat al-shahāda) has preceded in detail in al-Baqara, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ هُوَ الرَّحْمنُ الرَّحِيمُ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ): multiple predicates of Allah. The Most Beautiful Names of Allah have preceded.
(سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; عمّا is attached to سبحان; and the clause يشركون is the ṣila.
(هُوَ اللَّهُ الْخالِقُ الْبارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ): هو is a mubtadaʾ, and the Most Beautiful Names after it are predicates.
(لَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى): له is a fronted khabar, الأسماء a postponed mubtadaʾ, and الحسنى an adjective. الحسنى is the feminine of الأحسن, which is an elative (ism tafḍīl), not the feminine of أحسن as counterpart to امرأة حسناء. In al-Qāmūs: «Do not say رجل أحسن as counterpart to امرأة حسناء; its reverse is غلام أمرد, but do not say جارية مرداء. One only says هو الأحسن intending the elative afʿal, its plural being أحاسن; and الحسنى, with ḍamma, is the opposite of السوءى.»
(يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): this has preceded at the beginning of the sura.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ولتنظر نفس ما قدّمت لغد» there is the indefiniteness of نفس and of غد. As for the indefiniteness of نفس, it expresses the fewness of the souls that look into what they have sent ahead for the Hereafter. As for the indefiniteness of غد, it is to magnify it and leave its matter vague, as if it were said: for a tomorrow whose true nature is not known because of its greatness.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَخْرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِن دِيَارِهِمْ﴾.
These are the Banū al-Naḍīr. They had made a pact with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they would be neither with him nor against him. When the Muslims suffered their setback on the day of Uḥud, they acted treacherously: Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab rode to Abū Sufyān and his companions among the people of Mecca, and they made a pact against the Prophet ﷺ. Revelation came to him about that, and he said to the Muslims: "I have been commanded to kill Ḥuyayy." A party of the Muslims volunteered for it and killed him. The Prophet ﷺ went out against them in the morning, and they fortified themselves in their houses; they began boring through (the walls of) one house into another that was better fortified, and pelting the Prophet ﷺ with the stones they took out of it; and the Muslims began demolishing their houses to widen the place of fighting. That is His saying [Mighty and Majestic]: ﴿يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِي ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. The readers agreed on (يُخْرِبون), except ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who read (يخرّبون). «يخرّبون» is as it were «يهدّمون» (they demolish), and «يُخْرِبون», without shadda, means: they go out of them and leave them (deserted). Do you not see that they were boring through the houses and so leaving them unusable? That is the meaning of (يُخْرِبون). Those who said (يخرّبون) took it in the sense of the demolition the Muslims were carrying out. All of it is correct, and the agreed reading of the readers is dearer to me.
«[Translator's note: the reader is elsewhere called «أبو عبد الرحمن السلمى»; the source here has «عبدالرحمن السلمى».]»
[And His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَٱعْتَبِرُواْ يٰأُوْلِي ٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾: O possessors of minds. And it is said: «يا أولى الأبصار» means: O you who witnessed that with your own eyes.]
And His saying: ﴿لأَوَّلِ ٱلْحَشْرِ ﴾.
[They were] the first to be expelled from the Arabian peninsula, which is the Hijaz.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا قَطَعْتُمْ مِّن لِّينَةٍ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the Prophet ﷺ ordered all the palm trees to be cut down that day — meaning the day of the Banū al-Naḍīr — except the ʿajwa. Ibn ʿAbbās said: every kind of palm other than the ʿajwa is «اللين».
Al-Farrāʾ said: its singular is «لِينة». In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ما قطعتم من لِينَةٍ ولا تركتم قُوَّماً على أصوله إلا بإذن الله"; He is saying: except by the command of Allah.
And His saying: ﴿أُصوله﴾.
He took «اللين» as a whole collectively (with a masculine pronoun); and whoever said «أُصُولها» took «النخل» as feminine, because it is treated as masculine and feminine.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَآ أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ وَلاَ رِكَابٍ﴾.
The Prophet ﷺ had secured the spoils of Banū al-Naḍīr, Qurayẓa and Fadak. The chiefs said to him: "Take your choice portion of this and allot us the fourth." Then the explanation came: these are villages which they did not fight for with horses, and to which they did not travel on camels; you only walked to them on your feet — there were two miles between them and Medina. So the Prophet ﷺ gave them to some of the Emigrants who were in need and had been present at Badr.

farraa:7-7.t:
Then He said: ﴿مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾.
These three; it belongs purely to Allah and the Messenger.
Then He said: ﴿وَلِذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾:
for the kin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ﴿وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ﴾: the orphans of the Muslims in general, among them the orphans of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; ﴿وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾: the poor of the Muslims, not including the poor of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
Then He said: «كَىْ لا يَكُونَ ذلك الفَىء دُولة بين الأغنياء» — the chiefs — to be dealt with as it was dealt with in the Jāhiliyya. And concerning the chiefs there came down: ﴿وَمَآ آتَاكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَٱنتَهُواْ﴾, and they were content. As for «الدُّولة», the people read it with a ḍamma on the dāl, except al-Sulamī — as far as I know — who read «دَولة» with a fatḥa. This is not the place for «الدَّولة»: «الدَّولة» applies to two armies, where this one routs that one and then the victor is routed, so you say: «the turn (al-dawla) has come back against these», as though it were a single occasion. «الدُّولة» applies to possession (of wealth) and to customs that change and alternate over time; that is «الدُّولة».
Some of the Arabs read (دولةٌ) (nominative), but most of them read it accusative; and some (read) «يكون», and some «تكون».

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُوا ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلإِيمَانَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
He means the Anṣār, who love those who emigrated to them. When the Emigrants were given what the Prophet ﷺ apportioned to them of the spoils (fayʾ) of the Banū al-Naḍīr, he did not feel sure that others would not envy them, since he had not apportioned anything to them. So the Prophet ﷺ said to the Anṣār: "If you wish, you will share with them from your houses and your property, and I will apportion to you as I have apportioned to them; or else the share will be theirs, and you keep your houses and your property." They said: "No; rather you apportion to them from our houses and our property, and we will not share with them in the allotment." So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed these verses in praise of the Anṣār, saying: ﴿يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ — meaning the Emigrants — ﴿وَلاَ يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ﴾ to the end of the verse.

farraa:10-10.t: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ — meaning the Emigrants — (continues): «يقولون ربَّنا اغفِرْ لنا ولإخواننا الذين تبوءوا الإيمان من قبل، وألّف بين قلوبنا، ولا تجعل فيها غَمَرا للذين آمنوا» (they say: our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who settled in faith before, unite our hearts, and put in them no rancour towards those who believe).

farraa:13-14.t:
His saying: ﴿لأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً فِي صُدُورِهِمْ﴾.
He is saying: you, O company of Muslims, are more feared in their breasts [meaning the Banū al-Naḍīr] than the punishment of Allah is in their view. That is because the Banū al-Naḍīr were people of might, but Allah cast terror of the Muslims into their hearts. Concerning that came down: ﴿تَحْسَبُهُمْ﴾ — meaning the Banū al-Naḍīr — united, while their hearts differ. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وقلوبهم أشت», that is: more divided.
«[Translator's note: «جيمعاً» in the source is a misprint for «جميعاً».]»
And His saying: ﴿أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ جُدُرٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «جدار» (a wall), and the rest of the readers «جدر» in the plural.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَانَ عَاقِبَتَهُمَآ أَنَّهُمَا فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَالِدِينَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «فكان عاقبتهُما أنهما خالدان فى النار» (nominative). In [196/ب] our reading ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ is accusative. I do not like the nominative, even though it is permissible. That is because the adverbial phrase (ṣifa) has referred back to the Fire twice, and the meaning is about the abiding. So when you see the (participial) predicate between two adverbial phrases, one of which refers back to the place of the other, you put the predicate in the accusative; and this is of that kind. Similar in speech is your saying: «مررت برجل على بابه متحملا به» (I passed a man at whose door (someone was) loading up at it). Similar is the poet's saying:
والزعفرانُ على ترائبُها * شَرِقاً به اللباتُ والنحْرُ
(And saffron is on her breast-bones, her upper chest and throat drenched with it.)
For «الترائب» here are «اللبات», so the adverbial phrase came back with its noun on which it fell first. But when the two adverbial phrases differ, both the nominative and the accusative are permissible and good. Of that is your saying: «عبدالله فى الدار راغبٌ فيك» (ʿAbd Allāh is in the house, desiring you).
Do you not see that the «فى» in «فى الدار» differs from the «فى» that goes with the desire? The proof by which the accusative is distinguished from the nominative is: do you see (whether) the latter phrase can come before the first? Thus you say: «هذا أخوك فى يده درهم قابضا عليه» (this is your brother, in his hand is a dirham, grasping it); but if you said «هذا أخوك قابضاً عليه فى يده درهم», it would not be permissible. And you say: «هذا رجل فى يده درهم قائمٌ إلى زيد» (this is a man with a dirham in his hand, standing towards Zayd); do you not see that you can say «هذا رجل قائم إلى زيد فى يده درهم»? So this indicates the accusative when putting the latter (phrase) first is impossible, and indicates the nominative when putting the latter first is easy.
«[Translator's note: in the verse the source prints «ترائبُها» with a ḍamma; the genitive «ترائبِها» is expected after «على».]»

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَوِيۤ أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ولا أصحاب النار»; «لا» is a ṣila (redundant connective) when there is a negation at the beginning of the statement and it is connected by «لا» at its end. One of the Banū Kilāb recited:
إرادة ألاّ يجمع الله بيننا * ولا بينها أخرى الليالى الغوابر
(Wishing that Allah should not bring us together, nor her, until the last of the remaining nights.)
Its meaning is: wishing that Allah should not bring us and her together; so he connected with «لا».
«[Translator's note: «وأنشد فى بعض بنى كلاب» is as printed, evidently for «وأنشد بعض بنى كلاب».]»

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent); the clause «وهو العزيز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «هو الذي» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «كفروا»; the preposition phrase «من ديارهم» is attached to «أخرج»; it is permissible for two identical particles to be attached to one governing word because their meanings differ: the first is for clarifying the genus and the second for the beginning of the extent. The preposition phrase «لأول» is attached to «أخرج», and it is the lām of timing, i.e.: at the first gathering; the clause «ما ظننتم» is resumptive, and أنَّ with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «ظن»; the clause «وظنوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما ظننتم»; «حصونهم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «مانعتهم». The preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to «مانعتهم»; the clause «فأتاهم» is conjoined to the clause «ظنوا». «حيث» is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of a genitive, attached to «أتاهم»; the clause «لم يحتسبوا» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «يخربون» is resumptive, and the clause «فاعتبروا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «أَنْ» with what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "موجود" (existing); the preposition phrase «في الآخرة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عذاب»; the clause «ولهم عذاب» is resumptive and is not conjoined to the apodosis clause, because if you conjoined it, it would entail that punishment is withheld from them in the Hereafter, whereas the punishment in this world is withheld because of the occurrence of the exile.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أنَّ» and what follows it is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the conditional clause is resumptive; «من» is a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «يشاق» is the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «ما» is a conditional noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition phrase «من لينة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ما»; «قائمة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ. The preposition phrase «على أصولها» is attached to «قائمة»; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); the preposition phrase «بإذن» is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: so their cutting was by Allah's permission (فَقَطْعُها بإذن الله); the genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «وليخزي» is attached to an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e.: and He permitted their cutting in order to disgrace; the implied clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما قطعتم».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «وما أفاء» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {مَا قَطَعْتُمْ}; «ما» is a conditional noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أفاء»; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); «ما» is negative; «خيل» is the mafʿūl bihi of «أوجف», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «ولكن الله ...» is conjoined to the clause «ما أفاء الله»; the clause «والله قدير» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «على كل» is attached to «قدير».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «ما» is conditional, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition phrase «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أفاء»; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); the preposition phrase «لله» is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: then it is for Allah (فهو لله); «كي» is an infinitival and subjunctive-governing particle, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām; the adverb «بين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «دولة»; the preposition phrase «منكم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأغنياء». The clause «وما آتاكم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما أفاء الله»; «ما» in his words «ما آتاكم» is conditional, mafʿūl bihi; the clause «وما نهاكم» is conjoined to the clause «آتاكم الله»; «ما» in «وما نهاكم» is a mubtadaʾ and not an object, because the verb «نهاكم» has taken its full object.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition phrase «للفقراء» is a badal (substitute) from his words {وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَى} and what follows it; what prevented substitution from «لله وللرسول» is that it is obligatory to magnify them both; the clause «يبتغون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «أخرجوا»; the preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) «فضلا»; «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The wāw is resumptive; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «يحبون», and the clause is resumptive. His words «والإيمان»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الدار»; the verb is made to include the meaning of «لزموا» (they adhered to), so that conjoining «الإيمان» to it is sound, since faith is not something one settles in; the preposition phrase «من قبلهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause «يحبون» is the khabar of «الذين»; the preposition phrase «في صدورهم» is attached to the second object of «وجد»; the preposition phrase «مما» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «حاجة»; the wāw in «ولو» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause «لو كان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; this wāw conjoins to an implied (muqaddar) ḥāl for exhaustiveness, i.e.: they prefer [others] in every state, even in this state. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it; the clause «ومَنْ يوق» is parenthetical; «مَنْ» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «يوق» is the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «والذين جاءوا..» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «الذين تبوءوا ...»; the clause «ولا تجعل» is conjoined to the clause «اغفر»; the preposition phrase «في قلوبنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object; «للذين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «غِلا»; the clause «ربنا» is a resumption within the scope of the saying; and the clause «إنك رءوف», the answer to the vocative, is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «يقولون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين»; the preposition phrase «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from the wāw in «كفروا»; the clause «لئن أُخرجتم» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); «أبدًا» is an adverb of time attached to «نطيع»; the clause «لننصرنَّكم» is the answer to the oath, and before «إنْ» there is an implied (muqaddar) lām; the clause «إنهم لكاذبون» is the answer to the oath, on the basis that «يشهد» is made to include the meaning of an oath; the hamza of «إنَّ» takes kasra because of the lām in its khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «لا يخرجون» is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, the answer to the oath indicating it. His words «ليُوَلُّن»: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was omitted because of a succession of identical letters; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent); «الأدبار» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause «لا ينصرون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ليولن».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (لأنتم أشد رهبة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām is of inception (ibtidāʾ); «رهبة» is tamyīz (specification); the preposition phrase «في صدورهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رهبة»; the preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to «أشدّ»; the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to the khabar (predicate); and the clause «لا يفقهون» is a naʿt of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «لا يقاتلونكم» is resumptive; «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يقاتلون»; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the preposition phrase «في قرى» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the preposition phrase «من وراء» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preposition phrase «في قرى», attached to what it is attached to; the clause «بأسهم شديد» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «تحسبهم»; and the clause «وقلوبهم شتى» is a ḥāl clause from the hāʾ in «تحسبهم».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The preposition phrase «كمثل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: their likeness is as the likeness (مثلهم كمثل); «قريبا» is an adverb of time attached to «ذاقوا»; and the clause «ولهم عذاب» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ذاقوا».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «كمثل» is parsed like its counterpart in the previous verse; «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قال»; the preposition phrase «منك» is attached to «بريء»; the clause «إني أخاف» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «فكان» is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the noun of kāna; «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar (predicate); and the clause «وذلك جزاء» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «الذين» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the clause «ولتنظر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «اتقوا»; «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «ولا تكونوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause {اتَّقُوا}; the clause «فأنساهم» is conjoined to the clause «نسوا»; «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «أصحاب الجنة ...» is resumptive; «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «خاشعا متصدعا» are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the hāʾ; the preposition phrase «من خشية» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متصدِّعا»; the clause «نضربها» is the khabar (predicate); and the clause «لعلهم يتفكرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of the Divine Name; «عالم» is a naʿt of the Divine Name; the clause «هو الرحمن» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of the Divine Name; the clause of transcendence [«لا إله إلا هو»] is the ṣila (relative clause); «هو» is a badal (substitute) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar (predicate); «الملك» and what follows it are attributes of the Divine Name; the preposition phrase «عمَّا» is composed of the preposition «عن» and the maṣdariyya (infinitival) «ما», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) governor that puts «سبحان» in the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: His words «هو الله»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and what follows it are naʿts (adjectives) of the Divine Name; the clause «له الأسماء» is a second khabar of the Divine Name; the clause «يسبح» is resumptive; the clause «وهو العزيز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, and «الحكيم» is a second khabar.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying, Exalted is He, من خيل وَلَا ركاب: in ordinary speech ولا ركابا in the accusative is permissible, conjoining it to the position of من خيل, because من is redundant (zāʾida) and خيل is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying كي لَا يكون دولة: دولة is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and in كان is its noun; its implied form is "so that the spoils may not be a circulation" (كي لا يكون الفيء دولة). Whoever reads تكون with the تاء and دولةٌ in the nominative makes it the noun of كان, with كان meaning "occur", needing no khabar. لا in both readings is not redundant.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying يَبْتَغُونَ فضلا من الله: يبتغون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الفقراء and of the pronoun in أخرجوا.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying وَالَّذين تبوءوا الدَّار: الذين is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الفقراء, and يحبون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الذين; like it are ولا يجدون and ويؤثرون. Or [الذين is] in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being يحبون.
His saying كَمثل الشَّيْطَان: the كاف is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the likeness of these is like the likeness of Satan" (مثل هؤلاء كمثل الشيطان).
His saying لَا يخرجُون مَعَهم وَلَا ينصرونهم: they are not jussive because they are the answers to two oaths before them, and the condition did not govern them.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying لَا يقاتلونكم جَمِيعًا: جميعا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nominative latent pronoun.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying فَكَانَ عاقبتهما أَنَّهُمَا فِي النَّار: أنّ is in the position of the nominative as the noun of كان, and العاقبة is the khabar (predicate); خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial). خالدان in the nominative is permissible as the khabar of أنّ, with the adverbial phrase made non-functioning (mulghā), and al-Aʿmash read thus. Both ways are equal according to Sībawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: the accusative of خالدين as a ḥāl is preferable, so that the adverbial phrase is not made non-functioning twice, in في النار and فيها. According to al-Farrāʾ nothing is permissible but the accusative of خالدين as a ḥāl, because if you put خالدين in the nominative as the khabar of أنّ, the right of في النار would be to come later, so the pronoun would precede the overt noun, since the implied form according to him becomes "so their end was that they were abiding in it, in the Fire" (فكان عاقبتهما أنهما خالدان فيها في النار). This is permissible according to the Basrans when the pronoun comes after the overt noun in the wording, even if the rank of the overt noun is to come later; according to them only the wording is regarded. All of them permitted ضرّ زيدا طعامُه ("his food harmed Zayd"), because the pronoun comes later in the wording, even though its rank is to come first, since it is the agent.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying خَاشِعًا متصدعا: two ḥāls (circumstantial) of the هاء in رأيته, and رأيت is from seeing with the eye.
His saying المصور: it is مُفَعِّل from صوّر يصوّر; it is not good for it to be from صار يصير, because it would then have to be said المصيِّر with a yāʾ. It is a naʿt (adjective) after a naʿt, or a khabar (predicate) after a khabar. Its accusative is permissible in ordinary speech, but the wāw must then have a fatḥa, and you make it accusative by البارئ, i.e. "He is Allah, the Creator, the Maker of the fashioned one", meaning Adam, upon him be peace, and his children. Its accusative with a kasra on the wāw is not permissible, because [it would then be] an object. It is related from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read with a fatḥa on the wāw and a kasra on the رآء, by analogy with الحسنِ الوجهِ ("the handsome of face"). [Translator's note: the text says «لِأَنَّهُ مفعول» ("because it is an object"); the sense appears to be that with a kasra on the wāw المصوِّر is an agent noun, not something fashioned, so it cannot be the object of البارئ.]

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿هو الذي أخرج الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب من ديارهم﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or it is circumstantial (a ḥāl); هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿أخرج﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position. من أهل الكتاب is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذين كفروا, and من ديارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخرج﴾.
﴿لأول الحشر﴾: this lām is attached to ﴿أخرج﴾, and it is the lām of timing (lām al-tawqīt).
﴿ما ظننتم أن يخرجوا﴾: ما is negative; ظننتم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; يخرجوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; and أن together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of ظننتم.
﴿وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ظنوا is a past verb, one of the verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb), and the wāw is the fāʿil; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism); مانعتهم is the khabar of أنهم, and حصونهم is the fāʿil of مانعتهم; or مانعتهم is a fronted khabar and حصونهم a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of أنهم; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مانعتهم﴾; and the clause ﴿أنهم مانعتهم ...﴾ stands in place of the two objects of ظنوا.
﴿فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب﴾: the fāʾ is for conjunction with immediate sequence (taʿqīb); أتاهم الله is a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and a postponed fāʿil; من is a preposition, and حيث is an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by من, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أتاهم; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يحتسبوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; and the clause is in the position of a genitive through the adverb's being annexed to it; قذف is conjoined to فـ﴿أتاهم﴾; في قلوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قذف; and الرعب is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿يخربون بيوتهم بأيديهم وأيدي المؤمنين﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in قلوبهم; يخربون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; بيوتهم is the mafʿūl bihi; بأيديهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يخربون﴾; أيدي is conjoined to بأيديهم; and المؤمنين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اعتبروا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; يا is a vocative particle; أولي is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative by the yāʾ, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; and الأبصار is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ولولا أن كتب الله عليهم الجلاء لعذبهم في الدنيا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لولا is a particle of non-occurrence due to existence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd); أن is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما﴾ and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "existing" (موجود) [Translator's note: the source writes ﴿ما﴾ here, but the maṣdar-forming particle in this phrase is أن]; كتب الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كتب﴾; الجلاء is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا; عذبهم is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi; في الدنيا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عذبهم﴾; and the clause ﴿ولولا أن كتب...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ولهم في الآخرة عذاب النار﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لهم is a fronted khabar; في الآخرة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from عذاب; عذاب النار is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause ﴿ولهم في الآخرة...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and بأنهم is the khabar (predicate) of ذلك; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism), and the clause شاقوا is its khabar; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and رسوله is conjoined to the Word of Majesty.
﴿ومن يشاق الله فإن الله شديد العقاب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ; يشاق is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the Word of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "He will punish" (يعاقب); the fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya); إن is an abrogating particle, the Word of Majesty is its noun, and شديد is its khabar. You may also make the fāʾ the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and the clause is then in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis; and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ما قطعتم من لينة أو تركتموها قائمة على أصولها فبإذن الله﴾: ما is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿قطعتم﴾; قطعتم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); من لينة is a ḥāl (circumstantial); أو is a conjunction; تركتموها is conjoined to قطعتم; قائمة is the second object of ﴿ترك﴾; على أصولها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قائمة﴾; the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; بإذن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "so cutting them is by Allah's permission" (فقطعها بإذن الله); and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿وليخزي الفاسقين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and what it is conjoined to is omitted, its implied form being "He permitted cutting them, to gladden the believers and strengthen them, and to disgrace the hypocrites and the transgressors and abase them"; the lām is the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); يخزي is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted and supplied; and الفاسقين is the object of يخزي.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وما أفاء الله على رسوله منهم فما أوجفتم عليه من خيل ولا ركاب﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ما is a relative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause أفاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. الله is the fāʿil (agent); على رسوله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أفاء﴾; منهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); ما is negative; أوجفتم is a verb and its fāʿil; عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أوجفتم﴾; من is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and خيل is genitive by من in form and accusative in position, as the object of أوجفتم; and لا ركاب is conjoined to خيل.
﴿ولكن الله يسلط رسله على من يشاء﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) that governs the accusative; the Word of Majesty is its noun (ism), and the clause يسلط is its khabar (predicate); رسله is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يسلط; على من يشاء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يسلط﴾; and the clause يشاء is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿والله على كل شيء قدير﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدير﴾; and قدير is the khabar of the Word of Majesty الله.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ما أفاء الله على رسوله من أهل القرى﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ما is a relative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause أفاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. الله is the fāʿil (agent); على رسوله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أفاء﴾; and من أهل القرى is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أفاء﴾.
﴿فلله وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), because of the sense of condition contained in the relative noun; لله is the khabar (predicate) of ما; and للرسول and what follows it are conjoined to His words لله.
﴿كي لا يكون دولة بين الأغنياء منكم﴾: كي is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle before which the lām is supplied; لا is negative; يكون is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by كي; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿كي لا يكون﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by an omitted lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar to which the preposition and genitive noun ﴿لله﴾ are attached, or they are attached to an omitted verb, the implied form being "Allah made the fayʾ thus, so that it would not be a circulation" (جعل الله الفيء كذلك لكي لا يكون دولة); the noun (ism) of يكون is latent (mustatir), referring back to the fayʾ; دولة is the khabar of يكون; بين is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of دولة; الأغنياء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb indicated by خذوه. Or ﴿ما﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause فخذوه is the khabar; the clause أتاكم is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The kāf is the mafʿūl bihi and الرسول is the fāʿil; the fāʾ is linking; and خذوه is an imperative verb, its fāʿil, and its mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا﴾: conjoined to what precedes.
﴿واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil, and the Word of Majesty as object; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Word of Majesty is its noun, and شديد is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) from His words لذي القربى and what is conjoined to it; it has also been said: they are a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, its implied form being "marvel" (أعجبوا) [Translator's note: written thus in the source; the intended implied verb is presumably اعجبوا, "marvel (at)"]; المهاجرين is a naʿt (adjective) of الفقراء, and الذين is a second naʿt; the clause أُخرجوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; it is a past verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); من ديارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخرجوا﴾; and أموالهم is conjoined to ديارهم.
﴿يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا﴾: the clause is circumstantial (a ḥāl); فضلًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يبتغون﴾, or to an omitted naʿt of ﴿فضلًا﴾; and رضوانًا is conjoined to ﴿فضلًا﴾.
﴿وينصرون الله ورسوله﴾: the clause is conjoined to the clause يبتغون; the Word of Majesty is the object of ينصرون; and رسوله is conjoined to الله.
﴿أولئك هم الصادقون﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ; الصادقون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, and that clause is the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; you may also make it conjoined (mansūq) to الفقراء. So on these two views الذين is either a mubtadaʾ (subject), or conjoined to الفقراء and thus in the position of a genitive (majrūr). The clause تبوءوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; الدار is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الإيمان is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "and they made sincere" (وأخلصوا), the conjunction then being a conjoining of clauses; it has also been said that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, or that it is accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿تبوءوا﴾ after this has been made to include the sense of "they held fast to" (لزموا); من قبلهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تبوءوا or to the supplied ألفوا ("they became familiar with") [Translator's note: the source here names the supplied verb as ألفوا, whereas above it gave it as وأخلصوا]; the clause يحبون is the khabar (predicate) of الذين; من is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause هاجر is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿هاجر﴾.
﴿ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يجدون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); في صدورهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يجدون﴾; حاجة is the mafʿūl bihi; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of حاجة; and the clause ﴿أوتوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة﴾: conjoined to what precedes; على أنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤثرون﴾; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لو is conditional; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿بهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of كان; and خصاصة is its postponed noun (ism).
﴿ومن يوق شح نفسه﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من is conditional, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يوق is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; it is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); and شح is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فأولئك هم المفلحون﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a second mubtadaʾ; المفلحون is the khabar of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, and that clause is the khabar of أولئك; the clause ﴿فأولئك﴾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of من; and the clause ﴿ومن يوق...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان﴾: الذين is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿جاؤوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. من بعدهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جاءوا﴾; the clause يقولون is the khabar (predicate) of الذين; ربنا is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf; اغفر is a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); لإخواننا is conjoined to لنا; الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of إخواننا; the clause ﴿سبقونا﴾ is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position. بالإيمان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سبقونا﴾.
﴿ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is of request (ṭalabiyya); تجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; في قلوبنا is in the place of the second object of تجعل, and غلًّا is its first object; and للذين is a naʿt of ﴿غلًّا﴾.
﴿ربنا إنك رءوف رحيم﴾: ربنا is the one addressed, a muḍāf; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its noun (ism); رؤوف is the first khabar of إن, and رحيم is its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿ألم تر إلى الذين نافقوا يقولون لإخوانهم الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); إلى الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تر﴾; the clause نافقوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿يقولون﴾ is resumptive, explaining what is being marvelled at, with no grammatical position; لإخوانهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يقولون﴾; الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of إخوانهم; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position. من أهل الكتاب is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿لئن أخرجتم لنخرجن معكم ولا نطيع فيكم أحدا أبدا﴾: the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of their speech; the lām is the lām that prepares for an oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is conditional; أخرجتم is a past verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the lām [of لنخرجن] is likewise of the answer to the oath; نخرجن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath; the apodosis of the conditional إن is omitted; معكم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ﴿نخرجن﴾; the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; نطيع is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), because it is conjoined to the clause ﴿لئن أخرجتم﴾; and so too His words: وإن قوتلتم; thus the object of their saying is three clauses. فيكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نطيع﴾ on the omission of a muḍāf; أحدًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أبدًا is an adverb (ẓarf) of the negation, also attached to ﴿نطيع﴾.
﴿وإن قوتلتم لننصرنكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional, and before it the lām that prepares for an oath has been omitted; قوتلتم is a past verb in the passive, in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; ننصرنكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the apodosis of إن is omitted; and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath.
﴿والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يشهد is the khabar (predicate); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), its hamza takes kasra because the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) occurs in its khabar; the hāʾ is its noun (ism), and كاذبون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿لئن أخرجوا لا يخرجون معهم﴾: the lām is the lām that prepares for an oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is conditional; أخرجوا is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named) [Translator's note: so in the source; أُخرجوا is in fact a past verb], and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); it is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath, which is the clause لا يخرجون; and معهم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخرجون﴾.
﴿ولئن قوتلوا لا ينصرونهم﴾: conjoined to what precedes; the lām prepares for an oath; إن is conditional; قوتلوا is an imperfect verb in the passive [Translator's note: so in the source; قوتلوا is in fact a past verb], and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; it is in the position of a jussive as the protasis; and the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath, which is the clause لا ينصرونهم.
﴿ولئن نصروهم ليولن الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون﴾: also conjoined. As for His words ليولن: the lām is of the answer to the oath; يولن is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent); الأدبار is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ثم is a conjunction; لا is negative; and ينصرون is an imperfect verb conjoined to يولن, nominative like it. The pronouns refer back to the Jews, or to the hypocrites.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله﴾: the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); أنتم is the mubtadaʾ (subject); أشد is the khabar (predicate); رهبة is a tamyīz (specification); في صدورهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed in أشد; and من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رهبة﴾.
﴿ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ, and بأنهم is the khabar; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism), and قوم is its khabar; and the clause لا يفقهون is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿لا يقاتلونكم جميعا إلا في قرى محصنة أو من وراء جدر﴾: لا is negative; يقاتلونكم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), with its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جميعًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); إلا is a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); في قرى is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقاتلونكم﴾, and the pronoun refers to the Jews; محصنة is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قرى﴾; أو is a conjunction; من وراء is conjoined to ﴿في قرى﴾; and جدر is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿بأسهم بينهم شديد تحسبهم جميعًا وقلوبهم شتى﴾: the clause is resumptive, explaining their state, and has no grammatical position; بأسهم is the mubtadaʾ (subject); بينهم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ﴿شديد﴾; شديد is the khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿تحسبهم...﴾ is also resumptive, with no grammatical position; تحسبهم is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت), and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; جميعًا is the second mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); قلوبهم is a mubtadaʾ and شتى its khabar; and the clause is circumstantial (a ḥāl).
﴿ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ; بأنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism), and قوم is its khabar; and the clause لا يعقلون is a naʿt of ﴿قوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿كمثل الذين من قبلهم قريبا ذاقوا وبال أمرهم﴾: in ﴿كمثل﴾ the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "their likeness is like the likeness of those…" (مَثَلُهم مِثْلُ مَثَل الذين); ﴿مثل﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and الذين is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿من قبلهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. قريبًا is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to the omitted notion of "being settled" (al-istiqrār) to which من قبلهم is attached; you may also attach it to ﴿ذاقوا﴾, and some attached it to a supplied muḍāf; ذاقوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and وبال أمرهم is the object.
﴿ولهم عذاب أليم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لهم is a fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; عظيم is a naʿt (adjective) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in this ayah is أليم, not عظيم]; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر﴾: in ﴿كمثل﴾ the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "their likeness is like the likeness of Satan" (مَثَلُهم مِثْلُ مَثَل الشيطان); ﴿مَثَل﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشيطان; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through the adverb's being annexed to it; للإنسان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قال﴾; and the clause ﴿اكفر﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿فلما كفر قال إني بريء منك﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "and he disbelieved" (فكفر); لما is a temporal adverb meaning "when" (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya), or a linking particle (rābiṭa) that includes the sense of condition; the clause كفر is in the position of a genitive through the adverb's being annexed to it; the clause قال has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the yāʾ is its noun (ism), and بريء is its khabar; and منك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿بريء﴾.
﴿إني أخاف الله رب العالمين﴾: the clause is a false justification of his disowning him, for otherwise he does not fear Allah; إن is an abrogating particle, the yāʾ is its noun, and the clause أخاف الله is its khabar; and رب العالمين is a badal (substitute) from the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla), or a naʿt (adjective) of it.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار خالدين فيها﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; عاقبتهما is its fronted khabar (predicate); أن and what falls in its scope is its postponed noun (ism); في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of أن; خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خالدين﴾.
﴿وذلك جزاء الظالمين﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the punishment; جزاء الظالمين is the khabar of ذلك; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; اتقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Word of Majesty is its object; the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; تنظر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; نفس is the fāʿil; ما is the object of تنظر; and the clause قدمت is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "it sent forward" (قدمته); and لغد is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قدمت﴾.
﴿واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون﴾: the command to fear Allah is repeated to emphasise it; the clause إن الله خبير بما تعملون gives the reason for the command to fear Allah; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Word of Majesty is its noun (ism), and خبير is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تكونوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the wāw is its noun (ism); in ﴿كالذين﴾ the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿تكون﴾; الذين is a relative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause نسوا الله is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. فأنساهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أنساهم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أنفسهم is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أولئك هم الفاسقون﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a second mubtadaʾ; الفاسقون is the khabar of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, and that clause is the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة﴾: لا is negative; يستوي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); أصحاب النار is the fāʿil (agent); and أصحاب الجنة is conjoined to أصحاب النار.
﴿أصحاب الجنة هم الفائزون﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; أصحاب الجنة is the mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a second mubtadaʾ; and الفائزون is a khabar (predicate) in either case.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; لو is conditional; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); هذا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); القرآن is a badal (substitute); and على جبل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾.
﴿لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله﴾: the lām links the apodosis of لو; رأيته is a verb, its fāʿil, and its mafʿūl bihi; خاشعًا is a second object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing may be either mental or visual; متصدِّعًا is a second ḥāl, or a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿خاشعًا﴾; and من خشية الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿متصدعًا﴾.
﴿وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس﴾: the wāw is resumptive; تلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject); الأمثال is a badal; the clause نضربها is the khabar (predicate); للناس is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نضربها﴾; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿لعلهم يتفكرون﴾: لعل is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing hope (tarajjī); ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism); and the clause يتفكرون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿هو الله الذي﴾: هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject); الله is the first khabar (predicate); and الذي is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: its noun (ism), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of لا together with its noun, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (al-ibtidāʾ); or a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar. The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿عالم الغيب والشهادة﴾: عالم is a naʿt of the name of Allah, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, or a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو; الغيب is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; الشهادة is conjoined by the wāw, genitive by the kasra; and the nominal clause ﴿هو الله﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.
﴿هو الرحمن الرحيم﴾: هو is a pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; الرحمن is a khabar, nominative by the ḍamma; الرحيم is a second khabar, nominative by the ḍamma; and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive, reinforcing what came before.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿هو الله الذي﴾: هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject); الله is the first khabar (predicate); and الذي is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: its noun (ism), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of لا together with its noun, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (al-ibtidāʾ); or a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar. The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر﴾: adjectives (nuʿūt) of the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla), or further khabars of the mubtadaʾ ﴿هو﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive, reinforcing what came before.
﴿سبحان الله عما يشركون﴾: سبحان is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. standing in for the absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb; the Word of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); عما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سبحان﴾; and the clause يشركون is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿هو الله الخالق البارئ المصور﴾: هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the Most Beautiful Names that follow it are khabars (predicates).
﴿له الأسماء الحسنى﴾: له is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; الأسماء is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and الحسنى is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض﴾: يسبح is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; له is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يسبح﴾, or in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) ما; ما is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as fāʿil; في السماوات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. الأرض is conjoined by the wāw, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; and the clause is in the position of a nominative as a further khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿هو﴾.
﴿وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: هو is a pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; العزيز is a khabar, nominative by the ḍamma; الحكيم is a second khabar, nominative by the ḍamma; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, or in the position of a nominative by conjunction with the one before it.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: «سبح» is a past verb; «لله»: the lām is a preposition and the Word of Majesty is a genitive noun, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبح»; and it has been said: the lām is redundant (ṣila). «ما» is the fāʿil (agent); «في السماوات» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [word] which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. «ما في الأرض» is conjoined to «ما في السماوات»; «هو» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «العزيز» is a first khabar (predicate), and «الحكيم» is a second khabar.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: I.e. in His retribution on whoever disobeys Him. الْحَكِيمُ in His management [of affairs]. هُوَ is the mubtadaʾ (subject), الْعَزِيزُ is its khabar (predicate), and الْحَكِيمُ is a naʿt (adjective) of العزيز; it may also be a second khabar.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
هُوَ الَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا i.e. in Muḥammad ﷺ, مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ of the Jews, and they are the Banū l-Naḍīr, مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ لِأَوَّلِ الْحَشْرِ. أوّل is declined as a triptote because it is in construct (muḍāf); had it stood alone, leaving it diptote would be more fitting, on the basis that it is a naʿt (adjective); and whoever makes it not a naʿt declines it fully. ما ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا: «أن» is in the position of an accusative by ظننتم, and together with its ṣila it stands in place of the two objects according to the grammarians — except Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], for Abū l-Ḥasan related to us from him that the second object is omitted. The same is said of وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ مانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ. فَأَتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا i.e. they did not think, from their saying: ما كان هذا في حسباني, i.e. in my reckoning (ẓann); and one does not say في حسابي, because it has no meaning here. The meaning of «لم يحتسبوا» may be "they did not know"; and likewise it is said concerning people's saying: حسيبه الله, i.e. the One who knows his news and the One who will requite him is Allah, Majestic and Mighty. And it is said that the meaning of your saying حسيبك الله is "Allah is sufficient for me against you", from their saying أحسبه الشيء when the thing suffices him. And it is said: حسيبك i.e. the one who takes account with you (muḥāsibuka), like شريب in the sense of مشارب. And it is said: حسيبك i.e. having power over you, and from it is وكان الله على كل شيء حسيبا.
وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ — and whoever says في قلوبهم الرّعب [Translator's note: i.e. al-ruʿub with ḍamma on the ʿayn, which the print does not show] brings it according to the original. يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ — and يخرّبون [is read] to express multiplicity (al-takthīr); Sībawayh related that faʿʿala may have the meaning of afʿala, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 471-
ومن لا يكرم نفسه لا يكرم
(And whoever does not honour himself will not be honoured)
 فَاعْتَبِرُوا يا أُولِي الْأَبْصارِ i.e. take admonition, and infer the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ from the fact that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is his helper, by what He shows you concerning His enemies, and from the truth of what he has told you. Its derivation is from عبر إلى كذا, when he crosses over to it; and al-ʿabra (the tear) is what passes over from the eye to the cheek. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: and their saying فلان عبر, i.e. he does deeds by which he bequeaths tears to his family. Concerning the meaning of يا أُولِي الْأَبْصارِ there are two views:
one of them is that it is from the sight of the eye, and the other that it is from the sight of the heart. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is nearer to correctness, because taking heed (al-iʿtibār) is only with the heart, and it is taking admonition and inferring from what has passed. For it has been said:
the Prophet ﷺ informed them of this, that it would happen, and it happened as he described; so you must take heed from this and other things, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرامَ إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ [al-Fatḥ: 27], and it was as He said. And He, exalted be His mention, said: سَيَصْلى ناراً ذاتَ لَهَبٍ [al-Masad: 3], that [came about]. And He said: وَلَنْ يَتَمَنَّوْهُ أَبَداً [al-Baqara: 95], and none of them wished for it. And likewise وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ [al-Zukhruf: 87], and they said that. And likewise وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ [al-Rūm: 3]. Likewise his saying ﷺ to ʿAmmār: "The transgressing party will kill you"; and his saying, peace be upon him, to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, on the day he wrote "From Muḥammad the Messenger of Allah" and they demanded that he erase it, and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, found that grievous; so the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "You will be made to face the like of it" — and it was as he said. Likewise his saying concerning Dhū l-Thudayya, "and whoever escapes from the Khawārij", and the matter was as he said. Likewise his saying concerning the dogs of al-Ḥawʾab, a precise statement; likewise his saying concerning the conquest of the white city [Translator's note: al-madīna al-bayḍāʾ, apparently referring to al-Madāʾin] and the conquest of Egypt, and he enjoined good treatment of its people. All of this is among what one takes heed from. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ [al-Māʾida: 67], and He protected him until he died on his bed. And He said: وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كَمَا اسْتَخْلَفَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ [al-Nūr: 55], and of those who were addressed by this, four were made successors: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them; and this agreed with his saying, may Allah bless him: "The caliphate after me is thirty [years]". And among what one takes heed from are his comparisons that cannot be refuted, among them the ḥadīth of Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah give life to the dead, and what is the sign of that in His creation?" He said: "O Abū Razīn, have you not passed by the valley of your people when it was barren, then passed by it stirring with green? Thus does Allah give life to the dead, and thus is His sign, the Exalted, in His creation." This is a dazzling comparison that cannot be matched; and so too his saying in comparing the dead person to one asleep and his resurrection to waking. This is the most similar of things to one another, and by this do the people of insight take heed.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The lexicographers related that one says: جلا القوم عن منازلهم and أجليتهم — this is the eloquent [usage]; Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab related أجلوا, and someone else related جلوا عن منازلهم يجلون; and "so-and-so was put in charge of al-jāliya and al-jālla" [Translator's note: i.e. the poll-tax levied on those who have left their homes]. Most people read — and it is the eloquent dialect well known from the speech of the Arabs, transmitted by the multitude through whom proof is established — وَلَوْلا أَنْ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْجَلاءَ with kasra on the hāʾ and ḍamma on the mīm [ʿalayhimu]. Among those who read it so are Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read عَلَيْهِمُ الْجَلاءَ with ḍamma on the hāʾ and the mīm [ʿalayhumu], and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read عَلَيْهِمُ الْجَلاءَ with kasra on the hāʾ and the mīm [ʿalayhimi]. [Translator's note: the print vowels all three identically; the described vowellings are given in brackets.] Abū Jaʿfar said: in the first reading the hāʾ is given kasra because of its adjacency to the yāʾ, since a ḍamma after a yāʾ was felt to be heavy; moreover, the end of the articulation of the hāʾ is at the articulation of the yāʾ. The mīm is given ḍamma because its original is ḍamma, so it was returned to its original. This is the clear reading. The second reading is according to the original, except that al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read عليهم [with ḍamma on the hāʾ] only when a quiescent letter meets the mīm; and it is not known from any of the readers, through a sound channel, that he read عليهم [ʿalayhum, with ḍamma, generally] except Ḥamza; then he departed from that and read فيهم [with kasra], and did not use ḍamma except in عليهم, إليهم and لديهم. Except that Ibn Kaysān argued for him in his singling out these three, saying: عليهم, إليهم and لديهم — the yāʾ in them is not a pure yāʾ; its origin is alif, because you say على القوم; for this reason they left it with its ḍamma, because the yāʾ's origin is alif; whereas the yāʾ in «في» is a pure yāʾ. He said: and I asked Abū l-ʿAbbās why al-Kisāʾī read عليهم with kasra on the hāʾ, but when he said (عليهمُ ال…) [Translator's note: i.e. before a quiescent letter] he gave it ḍamma? He said: he only gave it kasra following the yāʾ, because the kasra is the sister of the yāʾ; then when he was compelled to give the mīm ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters — because ḍamma is its original — it was more fitting that the hāʾ follow the mīm, so he gave it ḍamma, i.e. because its original is ḍamma and after it is something with ḍamma. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the best that has been said about this. As for the reading of Abū ʿAmr, عَلَيْهِمُ الْجَلاءَ [ʿalayhimi], there are two arguments for it. One of them is that he gave the mīm kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; this is an argument without sense, because one only gives kasra for the meeting of two quiescent letters to what has no original vowel; as for abandoning the original and bringing in another vowel, that is not permissible. The other argument is sound: he gave the hāʾ kasra only following the yāʾ, because he felt a ḍamma after a yāʾ to be heavy; and likewise he also felt a ḍamma after a kasra to be heavy, so he replaced it with a kasra by way of following (itbāʿ), as he had done with the hāʾ, and said عَلَيْهِمُ الْجَلاءَ [ʿalayhimi l-jalāʾa]. لَعَذَّبَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابُ النَّارِ i.e. along with the disgrace that overtook them in this world through the exile. Qatāda said: al-jalāʾ is going out from one land to another. And it is said: the meaning of كتب is "decreed", and it is figurative; and it is said: He wrote it in the Preserved Tablet.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
ذلِكَ may be in the position of a nominative on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that"; it may be in the position of an accusative, i.e. "We did that to them"; and it may also be in the position of a nominative, i.e. "that disgrace and the punishment of the Fire are theirs" بأنهم خالفوا الله ورسوله [Translator's note: so in the source; the muṣḥaf has بِأَنَّهُمْ شَاقُّوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ]. وَمَنْ يُشَاقِّ اللَّهَ: [يشاقّ is] in the position of a jussive by the condition, and the qāf is given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Fatḥa on it is permissible because of the heaviness of the doubling and the kasra; except that fatḥa is better when no quiescent letter meets it, as in مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ [al-Māʾida: 54], and when a quiescent letter meets it, kasra is better, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 472-
فغضّ الطّرف إنّك من نمير ... فلا كعبا بلغت ولا كلابا
(So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr: you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb)
 فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. His punishment is severe for whoever opposes Him and opposes His Messenger.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
Concerning the meaning of «اللّينة» there are three views from the exegetes. Sufyān narrated from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind from ʿIkrima ibn ʿAbbās [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās"], who said: al-līna is palm trees other than the ʿajwa; and this is the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrima, al-Zuhrī and Yazīd ibn Rūmān. The view of Mujāhid and ʿAmr ibn Maymūn [Translator's note: printed ʿUmar ibn Maymūn] is that it is all palm trees; and likewise Ibn Wahb narrated from Ibn Zayd, who said: al-līna is the palm trees, whether there were ʿajwa among them or not. Sufyān said: they are the choicest palm trees. These views are sound, because al-Aṣmaʿī related something like the first view; so it refers to all palm trees, and what they cut of them is specific, and so the views agree.
