According to a group of the scholars of Arabic, لينة is derived from اللون (colour), and the wāw changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it; and in the plural [one says] ليان, as [the poet] said: [al-Mutaqārib] 473-
وسالفة كسحوق اللّبا ... ن أضرم فيها الغويّ السّعر
(And a neck [tall] like the tallest of palms, in which the misguided one kindled the flame) [Translator's note: the verse as printed has اللّبان, whereas the argument requires الليان; it is translated as printed in the Arabic.]
 And some of them said: it is derived from لان يلين (to be soft); had it been from اللون, one would have said in the plural لو أن [Translator's note: so printed; presumably لِوان is intended]. وَلِيُخْزِيَ الْفاسِقِينَ i.e. and to abase whoever departs from obedience to Him, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
According to the exegetes this concerns the Banū l-Naḍīr, because no horses or camels were spurred against them; rather, they made peace on condition of exile, so Allah the Exalted gave possession of their property to the Prophet ﷺ to dispose of as he wished. Fadak was part of it. It is authentically reported from the Companions, among them ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ used to take from it what sufficed him and his family and put the remainder into weapons with which the enemy is fought, and into mounts. When the Prophet ﷺ died, Fāṭima, may Allah be pleased with her, claimed it as inheritance. Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said to her: "You are the dearest of people to me, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.' But I will maintain it according to what he used to do with it." His companions followed him in testifying that the Prophet ﷺ said thus, until that became a consensus; and the four caliphs acted upon it, changing nothing of it, and treated it as it had been treated in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. As for the meaning of "we are not inherited from; what we leave is charity", the scholars have spoken about it. Some of them said: the meaning of "we are not inherited from" is like the meaning of "I am not inherited from", just as an eminent man says: "We did such-and-such". And it is said: it applies to all the prophets, because none of them bequeathed any property; and they said: the meaning of خِفْتُ الْمَوالِيَ مِنْ وَرائِي [Maryam: 5] is: I feared that they would not act in obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
What shows this is وَاجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا [Maryam: 6]. And the meaning of يَرِثُنِي is prophethood and the law, and likewise وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمانُ داوُدَ [al-Naml: 16]. Concerning the meaning of "what we leave is charity" there are several views. Among the soundest of them is that it is in the status of charity, because he ﷺ did not own anything; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, only made this permissible for him, so he would spend from it on himself and on those he supported and put the remainder in the way of Allah. This is one view; and it is said:
rather, he had given in charity everything he owned. And it is said: «ما» has the meaning of الذي, i.e. "we are not inherited from [in] that which we left as charity", and the hāʾ was omitted because of the length of the noun. One says «وجف» when it hastens, and someone else أوجفه [made it hasten]. وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ i.e. as He gave him power over the Banū l-Naḍīr.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
On this verse there are four views. Among them: that it is the first fayʾ, and that whatever the Muslims receive by peace treaty without fighting, this is its ruling. And it is said: rather, this is other than the first, and this is the ruling for jizya and kharāj revenue, that it be divided; this is the view of Maʿmar. And it is said: rather, this is what was fought for against the people of war; this is the view of Yazīd ibn Rūmān. The fourth view is that this is the ruling for what horses and riding camels were spurred against and was fought for; this was its ruling until it was abrogated by the verse in Sūrat al-Anfāl. The correct view is that this ruling differs from the first, because it is authentically reported from those whose word constitutes proof that the first concerns the Banū l-Naḍīr and that its disposal was given to the Prophet ﷺ, while this second is otherwise, because in it is لِذِي الْقُرْبى وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ. What shows you this is the ḥadīth of ʿUmar, with the soundness of its isnad and the uprightness of its chain: it was read out to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Saʿīd, Yaḥyā ibn Mūsā and Hārūn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān [Translator's note: printed Mālik ibn Uways], from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The properties of the Banū l-Naḍīr were among what Allah gave as fayʾ to His Messenger, against which the Muslims spurred neither horses nor riding camels; so he used to spend from them on his family a year's provision, and what remained he put into weapons and mounts as equipment in the way of Allah." This shows that the ruling of the second verse differs from the ruling of the first, because the first shows that this was something for the Prophet ﷺ, and the second verse is otherwise. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ما أَفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرى فَلِلَّهِ — it is said: this is an opening of speech, and everything belongs to Allah; and the implied form is "then for the ways of Allah". وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبى: they are the Banū Hāshim and the Banū l-Muṭṭalib. وَالْيَتامى: they are those who have not reached puberty and whose fathers have died. وَالْمَساكِينِ: they are those whom the abasement of poverty has overtaken together with destitution. وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ: they are travellers, not on a journey of disobedience, who are in need. كَيْ لا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الْأَغْنِياءِ مِنْكُمْ: the pronoun in يكون refers back to ما, i.e. so that what Allah gave as fayʾ to His Messenger from the people of the towns does not become something circulating (dūla), passed around among the rich, who do with it as they like; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, divided it with this division. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read كي لا تكون دولة with the nominative and with «تكون» feminine: دولة is the noun (ism) of «تكون» and «بين الأغنياء» the khabar; and it may have the meaning of "occur", so that it needs no khabar, as in إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً [al-Baqara:
282, and al-Nisāʾ: 29]. «أغنياء» is the plural of غنيّ; this is how the weak [-final adjective] is pluralized, whereas if it is sound it is pluralized on fuʿalāʾ and fiʿāl, e.g. كريم, كرماء and كرام. The Arabs said, of the sound type, نصيب and أنصباء, likening it to the weak, and they also likened some of the weak to the sound: al-Farrāʾ related نفي and نفواء — with fāʾ — likened to the sound, and its yāʾ was changed into wāw. وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَما نَهاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا: some of the exegetes related that this concerns the spoils, and argued that al-Ḥasan said: "and whatever the Messenger gives you of the spoils, take it, and whatever he forbids you of embezzlement (ghulūl)". Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not show that the verse is specifically about it; rather, the verse is general. On this basis the Companions of the Messenger of Allah interpreted it: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said:
"Allah has cursed the woman who tattoos and the one who has herself tattooed, and the woman who plucks [facial hair] and the one who has it plucked." It was said to him: "We have read the Qurʾān and did not see this in it." He said: "The Messenger of Allah cursed them, and Allah said: وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَما نَهاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا." And from Ibn ʿAbbās there is something similar regarding the prohibition of making nabīdh in hollowed stumps (al-naqīr) and pitch-lined vessels (al-muzaffat). وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ i.e. beware of His punishment in your disobeying His Messenger. إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ i.e. His punishment is severe for whoever opposes His Messenger ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: لِلْفُقَراءِ الْمُهاجِرِينَ: it is said: it is a badal (substitute) for those mentioned before, with repetition of the particle, as in لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا [Saba': 32] لمن آمن منهم [Translator's note: the quoted wording is that of al-Aʿrāf: 75, لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ, although the source cites Sabaʾ: 32]. And it is said: the implied form is "so that it does not become something circulating among the rich among you, so that it is for the poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their properties", i.e. the polytheists drove them out. يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْواناً is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise وَيَنْصُرُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ. أُولئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
الَّذِينَ is in the position of a genitive, i.e. "for those who"; and it may be in the position of a nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ, i.e. who moved to them. If الذين is in the position of a genitive, يحبّون is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or cut off from what precedes it. وَلا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ حاجَةً مِمَّا أُوتُوا is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it, and likewise وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كانَ بِهِمْ خَصاصَةٌ, i.e. need for what they gave preference with. Every aperture or gap in a wall is a khaṣāṣa. وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ: jussive by the condition, and for that reason the alif has been dropped from it; and keeping it when it is a condition is not permissible according to the Basrans, but is permissible according to the Kufans, who likened it to the poet's saying:
474-
ألم يأتيك والأنباء تنمي
(Did it not reach you — and news spreads —)
 The difference between this and the first is that the alif never takes a vowel in any state, whereas the yāʾ and the wāw may take a vowel; this is a clear difference. But the Kufans mixed up the letters of prolongation and softness and gave them a single ruling, and went beyond that, from poetic licence, to permitting it in the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and in one of their views they interpreted Ḥamza's reading لا تخف دركا ولا تخشى [Ṭā Hā: 77] on this basis. The exegetes hold that al-shuḥḥ is taking property without right, and we have mentioned their views. What is well known in the speech of the Arabs is that al-shuḥḥ is more than al-bukhl (stinginess), and that one says شحّ فلان يشحّ when his stinginess becomes intense and he withholds surplus wealth, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 475-
ترى اللّحز الشّحيح إذا أمرّت ... عليه لماله فيها مهينا
(You see the mean miser, when it [the cup] is passed to him, treating his wealth with contempt for its sake)

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: الَّذِينَ may be in the position of a genitive, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes it, i.e. "and for those who"; and on this basis is the speech of the exegetes and the jurists, as Mālik said: whoever reviles the Companions of the Messenger ﷺ has no share in the fayʾ, because Allah the Exalted said: وَالَّذِينَ جاؤُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنا, the verse. Qatāda said: you were not commanded to revile the Companions of the Prophet; you were only commanded to seek forgiveness for them. Ibn Zayd said concerning the meaning of His saying وَلا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنا غِلًّا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: do not leave in our hearts rancour toward whoever was upon Your religion. رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ i.e. toward Your creation. رَحِيمٌ toward whoever of them repents.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ نافَقُوا: the alif is dropped for the jussive; its origin has a hamza, because it is from رأى, and the original is يرأى. يَقُولُونَ لِإِخْوانِهِمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ: «يقولون» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). From Ibn ʿAbbās: الَّذِينَ نافَقُوا are ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his companions, and their brothers among the People of the Book are the Banū l-Naḍīr. لَئِنْ أُخْرِجْتُمْ i.e. from your homes and dwellings, لَنَخْرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمْ from our homes. وَلا نُطِيعُ فِيكُمْ أَحَداً أَبَداً i.e. we will not obey whoever asks us to abandon you. وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ: إن is given kasra because of the coming of the lām; and ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he permitted fatḥa on it when its khabar has the lām, because the lām is for emphasis and so changes nothing here.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُوا لا يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ i.e. if the Banū l-Naḍīr are driven out, the hypocrites will not go out with them; so He informed of the unseen, and the matter was thus. وَلَئِنْ قُوتِلُوا لا يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ وَلَئِنْ نَصَرُوهُمْ لَيُوَلُّنَّ الْأَدْبارَ: so He, Majestic and Mighty, informed of what He knows. If it is said: what is the reason for the nominative in لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُوا لا يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ, when apparently it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and you say إن أخرجوا لا يخرجوا معهم and nothing else is permissible, while the lām is for emphasis — so why is the verb nominative? The answer to this — and it is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, according to their meaning — is that it is an oath. The meaning is: "By Allah, they will not go out with them if they are driven out", just as you say: "By Allah, they will not stand"; and the lām entered on the first because it is a condition for the second. Likewise what follows it; and likewise ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it, and it may be cut off from it.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: I.e. in the breasts of the Banū l-Naḍīr of the Jews; and رهبة is accusative as a tamyīz (specification). ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَفْقَهُونَ i.e. because they are a people who do not understand the measure of the majesty of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, so they are bold in disobeying Him and do not fear His punishment.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
جَمِيعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). According to al-Farrāʾ, قرية and [its plural] قرى is anomalous (shādhdh); its plural ought to have been قراء, like غلوة and غلاء. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq rejected this, and that something the Qurʾān has uttered should be called anomalous; rather, it is like ضيعة and ضيع, coming with the alif dropped.
And it is said: it is a collective noun. أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ جُدُرٍ بَأْسُهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ شَدِيدٌ: Abū ʿAmr [Translator's note: printed Abū ʿUmar] and Ibn Kathīr read أو من وراء جدار, and it is related from the Meccans أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ جُدُرٍ with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the dāl [Translator's note: i.e. jadrin; the print shows the vowelling of the standard reading]. And جدر [Translator's note: i.e. judr] is permissible on the basis that the original is جدر [judur], with the ḍamma dropped because of its heaviness. جدر [jadr] is a dialectal word meaning جدار (wall); and a single جدار conveys a plural, except that the plural better fits the arrangement of the verse, because before it is إِلَّا فِي قُرىً, and He did not say إلّا في قرية. تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعاً: [جميعا is] the second object of تحسب, and not a ḥāl. وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّى: Qatāda said: the people of falsehood have differing desires and differing deeds, while they are united in enmity toward the people of truth. Mujāhid said: وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّى because the Banū l-Naḍīr are Jews and the hypocrites are not Jews. In the codex (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd: وقلوبهم أشتّ, where afʿal has the meaning of fāʿil, or «من» is omitted from it. ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَعْقِلُونَ i.e. they do not understand what holds benefit for them as against what holds loss for them.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
كَمَثَلِ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ: the meaning is: their likeness is as the likeness of those before them when they persisted in disobedience and were destroyed. The exegetes disagreed about الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ here. Ibn ʿAbbās said:
they are the Banū Qaynuqāʿ; and Mujāhid said: they are the people of Badr. The correct thing to say about this is that the verse is general, and all of these are among those who were before them. قَرِيباً is a naʿt (adjective) of an adverb (ẓarf). ذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ i.e. they tasted the punishment of Allah for their disbelief and disobedience. وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ i.e. in the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
The kāf is in the position of a nominative, i.e. the likeness of the hypocrites in their deluding the Banū l-Naḍīr, and the likeness of the Banū l-Naḍīr in their hearts from them [Translator's note: so in the source, في قلوبهم منهم; presumably في قبولهم منهم, "in their accepting from them", is intended], is as the likeness of Satan. Concerning its meaning there are two views. One of them is that it is a particular devil who deluded a monk.
On this there is a ḥadīth with a chain of transmission that we have mentioned; and thus it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him.
The other view is that الشيطان here is a name for the genus, and likewise الإنسان, as Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: it is general.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
عاقِبَتَهُما is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and أنّ with its ṣila is its noun (ism). Al-Ḥasan read فَكانَ عاقِبَتَهُما with the nominative [Translator's note: i.e. ʿāqibatuhumā], making it the noun of كان, and he made it [the verb] masculine because its femininity is not real. خالِدَيْنِ فِيها as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The grammarians disagree about the adverbial phrase when it is repeated. Sībawayh said: "This is the chapter of that in which the mustaqarr [i.e. the adverbial predicate] is repeated for emphasis"; so according to his view we say: إن زيدا في الدار جالسا فيها and جالس, neither being preferred over the other. Someone else said: the preference is the accusative, so that the adverbial is not made inoperative twice. Al-Farrāʾ said: the accusative here is the speech of the Arabs. He said: you say هذا أخوك في يده درهم قابضا عليه; and the reason for the accusative being necessary, according to him, is that it may not be fronted because of the pronoun; but if you say هذا أخوك في يده درهم قابض على دينار, the nominative and accusative are both permissible. He recited, concerning what is in the accusative:
[al-Kāmil] 476-
والزّعفران على ترائبها ... شرقا به اللّبّات والنّحر
(And saffron upon her breast-bones, the upper chest and throat drenched with it)
 Abū Jaʿfar said: according to Sībawayh nothing follows from this distinction. Sībawayh said: if the repetition put [it] in the accusative, it would be accusative in your saying: عليك زيد حريص عليك. This is among the best and clearest of what has been said on this, because he showed that repetition does not govern anything. وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ: it is said:
by it are meant the Banū l-Naḍīr, because the arrangement of the verse concerns them; and every disbeliever is a wrongdoer.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ i.e. by performing His obligations and avoiding acts of disobedience to Him. وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ: the original is ولتنظر [Translator's note: i.e. wa-litanẓur, with kasra on the lām]; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness and its being joined to the wāw; i.e. let a soul look at what it has sent ahead for the Day of Resurrection, of good that saves it or evil that destroys it. The original of غد is غدو, and it sometimes occurs in its original form. Then it was repeated for emphasis, and He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
نسي may have the meaning of "to abandon", i.e. they abandoned obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. فَأَنْساهُمْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ: Sufyān said:
i.e. He made them forget the share of their own selves. Among the good things said about it is that the meaning is: when Allah punished them, He distracted them from thinking about the people of their religion or about those close to them, as He said: فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ [al-Baqara: 54].
أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ i.e. those who depart from obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: لا يَسْتَوِي i.e. are not equal. أَصْحابُ النَّارِ وَأَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ: in the codex (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd: ولا أصحاب الجنّة, where «لا» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمُ الْفائِزُونَ i.e. those who attained what they sought.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
مُتَصَدِّعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in alarm out of its reverence for the Qurʾān. مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ: by this He showed that whoever has the Qurʾān with him must be fearful, cautious, revering it, keeping it far from whoever opposes it.
وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثالُ نَضْرِبُها لِلنَّاسِ i.e. He makes them know by this. لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ and so yield to the truth.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: هُوَ is the mubtadaʾ (subject). Some Arabs make the wāw quiescent, and whoever makes it quiescent drops it here because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The name of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and الَّذِي is part of its description (naʿt). لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ is in the ṣila (relative clause), i.e. the One to whom alone divinity is fitting, because He is the Creator of everything, so divinity is His alone. عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ is a naʿt (adjective); and had the first been with alif and lām, the second would be accusative, and the genitive would be permissible. هُوَ الرَّحْمنُ الرَّحِيمُ: mercy from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is bounty and beneficence toward whomever He has mercy on.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: whoever uses the accusative says: إلّا إياه; and the Kufans permitted إلّاه on the basis that the hāʾ is in the position of an accusative, and they recited: [al-Basīṭ] 477-
فما نبالي إذا ما كنت جارتنا ... ألّا يجاورنا إلّاك ديّار
(We do not care, as long as you are our neighbour, that no one but you should live near us)
 Abū Jaʿfar said: this is an error according to the Basrans; no [attached] pronoun occurs after «إلّا», only a detached one, because of its difference; and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd recited: «ألّا يجاورنا سواك ديّار». الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ: a naʿt (adjective). الملك (the King) is derived from المُلك (sovereignty), and المالك (the Owner) is derived from المِلك (ownership). «القدّوس» is derived from القدس, which is purity, as Ḥassān ibn Thābit said: [al-Wāfir] 478-
وجبريل أمين الله فينا ... وروح القدس ليس له كفاء
(And Jibrīl, Allah's trustee among us — and the Holy Spirit, who has no equal)
 Kaʿb said: the Holy Spirit (rūḥ al-qudus) is Jibrāʾīl, peace be upon him. Abū Zayd said: al-Quds is Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and likewise al-Quddūs. Someone else said: Jibrāʾīl ﷺ was called "the spirit of Allah" because He created him without male or female; and from this ʿĪsā ﷺ was called "the spirit of Allah", Majestic and Mighty, because He created him without a male. And Allah is al-Quddūs, i.e. kept pure from what the polytheists attributed to Him. Abū l-Dīnār al-Aʿrābī read الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ with fatḥa on the qāf [Translator's note: i.e. al-qaddūs; the print shows ḍamma]. Abū Jaʿfar said: its counterpart in the speech of the Arabs comes with fatḥa, e.g. سمّور and شبّوط, and nothing has come with ḍamma except «السّبّوح» and «القدّوس», and these two have also been given fatḥa. السَّلامُ i.e. possessor of soundness from all defects. Al-salām in the speech of the Arabs applies in five ways: al-salām is greeting; al-salām is "blackness" of speech [Translator's note: so printed, السّواد; presumably السَّداد, "sound/appropriate speech", is intended] — Allah the Exalted said: وَإِذا خاطَبَهُمُ الْجاهِلُونَ قالُوا سَلاماً [al-Furqān: 63], where greeting is not meant; al-salām is the plural of salāma; al-salām in the sense of al-salāma, as you say اللّذاذ and اللّذاذة — «السلام» as a name of Allah is from this, i.e. the possessor of soundness; and al-salām is a sturdy tree, its singular being salāma. Abū Isḥāq said: it is so called because of its soundness from defects. الْمُؤْمِنُ: there are three views on it. Among them is that its meaning is the One who has made His servants safe from His injustice; and it is said: al-Muʾmin is the One who has made His friends safe from His punishment; and Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is al-Muʾmin because He confirms the truthfulness of His believing servants. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of this is that the believers will bear witness against people on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, will confirm their truthfulness. الْمُهَيْمِنُ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-Muhaymin is the Trustworthy; and with this chain he said: the Witness. Abū ʿUbayda said: al-Muhaymin is the Watcher, the Preserver. Abū Jaʿfar said: all of these are among the attributes of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: Allah witnesses the deeds of His servants, preserves them, is trustworthy over them, does not wrong them and does not diminish any of their deeds. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Abū l-ʿAbbās, who said: the original is مؤيمن — and there is nothing diminutive among the names of Allah the Exalted; it is only like مسيطر — the hamza was replaced by hāʾ because the hāʾ is lighter. الْعَزِيزُ i.e. Mighty in His retribution, the Unassailable, so that whoever He punishes cannot avenge himself on Him. الْجَبَّارُ: there are four views on it. Qatāda said: al-Jabbār is the One who compels (yujbiru) His creation to what He wills. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is an error according to the scholars of Arabic, because from this only مجبر comes, and faʿʿāl does not come from afʿala. And it is said: «جبّار» is from "Allah set His creation right (jabara)", i.e. provided for them and sufficed them; and this is a good view with no objection to it. And it is said: جبار is from "I set the bone and it mended", i.e. I straightened it after it had broken; so Allah the Exalted has set the hearts right so that they understand His proofs. And it is said: it is from their saying تجبّر النخل when the palm grows tall and out of reach of the hand, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 479-
أطافت به جيلان عند قطاعه ... وردّت عليه الماء حتّى تجبّرا
(Jīlān [i.e. its gardeners] went round it at its cutting and brought the water back to it until it grew tall)
 So He was called Jabbār because no one can reach Him. الْمُتَكَبِّرُ i.e. the One exalted above His creation. سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ: سبحان is accusative on the basis that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) derived from سبّحته, i.e. I declared Him transcendent and free of what the polytheists say. When you use it on its own it may be definite or indefinite: if you make it indefinite you decline it fully and say سبحانا; and if you make it definite, [it is a diptote], as [the poet] said: [al-Sarīʿ] 480-
أقول لمّا جاءني فخره ... سبحان من علقمة الفاخر
(I say, when his boasting reached me: how far removed [from glory] is ʿAlqama the boaster!)

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
هُوَ اللَّهُ الْخالِقُ الْبارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ: the meaning of "he created (khalaqa) the thing" is "he measured it out", as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 481-
ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبعض ... القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري
(You cut out what you have measured, while some people measure and then do not cut)
 Except that Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿArafa said: the meaning of "Allah created the thing" is that He determined it, originating it without any prior model, without increase or decrease; for this reason people have abandoned using it [of others]. This is the meaning of his statement. الْبارِئُ: it is said: the meaning of al-Bāriʾ is the Creator; this involves laxity, owing to the weakness in Arabic of whoever says it, or on the basis of being lax about it because al-Khāliq is before it. The real sense of this is that the meaning of "Allah brought forth (baraʾa) creation" is that He made them even and proportioned them. Do you not see the coherence of the speech: before it is "created", i.e. measured out, and after it "brought forth", i.e. proportioned and made even, and after it الْمُصَوِّرُ — the form comes after these two. It has been said that al-Muṣawwir is derived from صار يصير; had it been so, it would be with yāʾ; rather, it is derived from الصورة, which is the likeness (al-mithāl). لَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى: Abū Hurayra said, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah has ninety-nine names." يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ, because it indicates that it has an originator and a manager who has no equal; so by its very form it glorifies Allah, i.e. it declares Him transcendent above things. وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ i.e. in His retribution on whoever disbelieves in Him. الْحَكِيمُ in what He has created, because no flaw is seen in His wisdom; and it is said: al-Ḥakīm has the meaning of al-Ḥākim (the Judge).

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(لله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun that is the fāʿil (agent) of سبّح [Note: It has been said: the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and the Name of Majesty is the object of سبّح.]. (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ما. (في الأرض) attached to the ṣila of the second ما. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya)..
The clause «سبّح ... ما في السموات» has no grammatical position, being initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «هو العزيز ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the Name of Majesty.

safi-cedvel:2-4.t:
* I'rab:
(من أهل) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of كفروا. (من ديارهم) attached to (أخرج). (لأوّل) attached to (أخرج) [Note: The lām is called the lām of timing (lām al-tawqīt), i.e. "at the first gathering".. Al-Zamakhsharī said: It is like the lām in His saying, Exalted is He: يا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي, and your saying: "I came for (i.e. at) such-and-such a time".. The expression is of the kind of annexing the adjective to the noun it qualifies, i.e. He is the One who expelled those who disbelieved at the time of the first gathering.]. (ما) negative. (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle. (حصونهم) the fāʿil (agent) of the active participle مانعتهم. (من الله) attached to (مانعتهم), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "from Allah's punishment" [Note: (حصونهم) may be a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and (مانعتهم) an advanced khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of أنّ.]. (الفاء) a conjunction. (حيث) an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (أتاهم). (في قلوبهم) attached to (قذف). (بأيديهم) attached to (يخربون). (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition. (أولي) the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, since it is attached to (mulḥaq bi) the sound masculine plural.
The clause «هو الذي ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أخرج ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ما ظننتم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يخرجوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخرجوا..) is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of ظننتم.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم مانعتهم..) is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of ظنّوا.
The clause «ظنّوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ما ظننتم.
The clause «أتاهم الله ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ظنّوا.
The clause «لم يحتسبوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قذف ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أتاهم الله.
The clause «يخربون ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: It may be a ḥāl from the absent pronoun in (قلوبهم).].
The clause «اعتبروا ...» is in the position of the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "If this is the state of the disbelievers, then take a lesson from their condition".
The clause «يا أولى الأبصار ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
3- (الواو) resumptive. (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle. (عليهم) attached to (كتب). (اللام) occurring in the response of لولا. (في الدنيا) attached to (عذّبهم). (لهم) attached to an advanced khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب). (في الآخرة) a ḥāl from عذاب [Note: Or attached to the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) to which (لهم) is attached.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن كتب) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "موجود" (existing).
The clause «لولا كتابة الجلاء ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كتب ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «عذّبهم ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لهم ... عذاب» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: The clause was not conjoined to the apodosis because punishment in this world is precluded by the existence of the exile, but in the Hereafter it is not precluded; had the clause been conjoined to the apodosis, it would have entailed that punishment is precluded for them in the Hereafter.].
4- The reference in His saying (ذلك) is to the expulsion in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter..
(الواو) resumptive. (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم شاقّوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause.
The clause «شاقّوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «من يشاقّ ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption confirming the content of what preceded.
The clause «يشاقّ ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «إنّ الله شديد ...» has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation (taʿlīl) for the implied apodosis, i.e.: "Whoever opposes Allah, He will punish him, for Allah is severe in punishment."

* Morphology:
(2) مانعتهم: feminine of مانع, an active participle of the triliteral منع; its pattern is فاعل.
(حصونهم) plural of حصن, a noun for a fortified place; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn, and the pattern of حصون is فعول, with two ḍammas.
(3) الجلاء: an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral verb جلا. It contains ibdāl (substitution) of the wāw by hamza; its origin is جلاو: the wāw came at the end after a vowelless alif and was converted to hamza; its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
- The expulsion of Banū al-Naḍīr..
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, Banū al-Naḍīr made a treaty with him on the terms that they would be neither against him nor for him. When the Muslims were defeated on the day of Uḥud, they grew doubtful and broke the treaty. Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf went out with forty riders to Mecca and made an alliance with Abū Sufyān at the Kaʿba. So he ﷺ commanded Muḥammad ibn Maslama al-Anṣārī, who killed Kaʿb by stealth. Then the Prophet ﷺ went out against them with the army and besieged them for twenty-one nights, and approved the cutting down of their palm trees. When Allah cast terror into their hearts, they asked for peace, but he refused them anything but exile, on the terms that every three households could carry on one camel whatever of their goods they wished, except weapons. So they went into exile to Adhriʿāt and Arīḥāʾ in the land of Syria. This exile was the first of their gatherings; the middle of their gatherings was ʿUmar's, may Allah be pleased with him, expelling them from Khaybar to Syria; and the last of their gatherings is the Day of Resurrection.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governing word being قطعتم. (من لينة) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ما [Note: Or it is the tamyīz (specification) of ما.]. (أو) a conjunction, and the wāw in (تركتموها) is redundant (zāʾida), lengthening the vowel of the mīm (ishbāʿ). (قائمة) a ḥāl, accusative, from the absent pronoun that is the object [Note: It was not parsed as a second object because the meaning of transformation is absent.]. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (بإذن) attached to the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "فعلكم" (your doing) — or "قطعها" (its cutting). (الواو) a conjunction. (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl). (يخزي) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām, and the agent is "هو", referring to the Name of Majesty..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخزي..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, it and what it is conjoined to, i.e.: "Allah permitted their cutting so as to gladden the believers and to disgrace the transgressors".
The clause «قطعتم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تركتموها ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «(فعلكم) بإذن الله ...» is in the position of the jussive (fī maḥall jazm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يخزي ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
6- (الواو) a conjunction. (ما أفاء) like ما قطعتم. (على رسوله) attached to (أفاء), and likewise (منهم). (الفاء) connecting the apodosis. (ما) negative. (عليه) attached to (أوجفتم). (خيل) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi. (لا) redundant to emphasise the negation. (ركاب) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to خيل by the wāw, genitive in form. (الواو) a conjunction. (على من) attached to (يسلّط), and the agent of (يشاء) is a pronoun referring to the Name of Majesty. (الواو) a conjunction. (على كلّ) attached to the khabar (قدير).
The clause «ما أفاء الله ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ما قطعتم.
The clause «ما أوجفتم ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لكنّ الله يسلّط ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ما أفاء الله.
The clause «يسلّط ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «الله ... قدير» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of rectification (istidrāk).

* Morphology:
(5) لينة: a noun for the palm tree; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn. It has been said that the original ʿayn of the word is wāw, because it is from اللون (colour), and it was converted to yāʾ because of the kasra before it.. And it has been said that it is a yāʾ, from اللين (softness).
(6) أفاء: contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion); its analogy is like فاء.. See verse (226) of Sūrat al-Baqara.
(ركاب) a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own root; it is the camels that are ridden, its singular being راحلة; its pattern is فعال, with kasra.

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(ما أفاء ... من أهل) like ما أفاء ... منهم [Note: In the previous verse (6), and (ما) is a second object.
(2, 3) In verse (5) of the sūra, and ما is a mubtadaʾ.]
[Translator's note: The source note above appears to merge the texts of footnotes 1–3; the markers for footnotes 2 and 3 are the stray closing quotation marks after the two occurrences of "like ما قطعتم" below.]
(الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (لله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو". (الواو) a conjunction in the seven places, and the last one is resumptive. (اليتامى) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty — or to ذي — and likewise (المساكين، ابن). (كيلا) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, and a particle of negation; the noun of (يكون) is a pronoun referring to the fayʾ. (بين) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to a naʿt (adjective) of دولة. (منكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأغنياء. (ما آتاكم) like ما قطعتم». (الفاء) connecting the apodosis. (ما نهاكم) like ما قطعتم». (عنه) attached to (نهاكم). (فانتهوا) like فخذوه..
The clause «ما أفاء الله ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «(هو) لله ...» is in the position of the jussive (fī maḥall jazm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يكون دولة ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (كي).
The interpreted maṣdar (كيلا يكون..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the lām, attached to an omitted verb, i.e.: "He made the fayʾ thus so that it would not be ...".
The clause «آتاكم الرسول ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ما أفاء الله.
The clause «خذوه ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما نهاكم عنه ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause آتاكم الرسول.
The clause «نهاكم عنه ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «انتهوا ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the second condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله شديد ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
8- (للفقراء) a badal (substitute) for ذي القربى, with repetition of the preposition [Note: Or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اعجبوا" (wonder). The speech is then resumed anew.]. The wāw in (أخرجوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (من ديارهم) attached to the verb أخرجوا. (من الله) attached to (يبتغون). (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) for emphasis [Note: Or a detached pronoun as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الصادقون.. and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.]..
The clause «أخرجوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يبتغون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «ينصرون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يبتغون.
The clause «أولئك ... الصادقون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(7) دولة: a noun meaning "something circulated"; its pattern is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(نهاكم) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion): the original of the alif is yāʾ; it was vowelled after a fatḥa and converted to alif; of the class of فتح.
(انتهوا) contains iʿlāl by making vowelless (taskīn) and iʿlāl by deletion; its origin is انتهيوا, with a yāʾ before the wāw. The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless and the vowel was transferred to the hāʾ — iʿlāl by taskīn. Two sukūns met, on the wāw and the yāʾ, so the yāʾ was deleted to escape the two vowelless letters..
Its pattern is افتعوا.

* Rhetoric:
Disjunction (al-faṣl): in His saying, Exalted is He: ما أَفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ.
Disjunction is leaving a clause unconjoined to another; its opposite is conjunction (al-waṣl), which is conjoining some clauses to others. Since there is complete unity between this verse and the verse before it, the two verses were disjoined. Disjunction is in itself eloquence: someone was asked, "What is eloquence?" and he said:
"Knowing disjunction and conjunction."

* Benefits:
- The ruling on fayʾ:
The discussion of the ruling on spoils of war (ghanīma) has preceded at the opening of Sūrat al-Anfāl. As for the ruling on fayʾ, it belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his lifetime, to place it wherever he wished. He used to spend from it on his family their maintenance for a year, and put what remained into horses and weapons, as provision in the way of Allah. The scholars differed over fayʾ after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some said: It belongs to the imams after him. Al-Shāfiʿī has two views on it: one, that it belongs to the fighters; the second, that it is for the welfare of the Muslims, beginning with the fighters, then the most important of the interests, then the next most important. They differed over taking a fifth of fayʾ property: most of the people of knowledge held that a fifth is not taken from it, but all of it is spent on the welfare of all the Muslims. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, recited (ما أَفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرى) until he reached (للفقراء المهاجرين), up to His saying وَالَّذِينَ جاؤُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ, then said: "This has encompassed the Muslims generally." He said: "There is no Muslim on the face of the earth but that he has a right in this fayʾ, except those whom your right hands possess."

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (من قبلهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تبوّؤا) [Note: Or attached to the implied verb that governs الإيمان: "ألفوا الإيمان" (they became familiar with faith), the conjunction here being a conjoining of clauses.]. (إليهم) attached to (هاجر). (لا) negative. (في صدورهم) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (ممّا) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of حاجة, the returning pronoun being omitted; and the wāw in (أوتوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (على أنفسهم) attached to (يؤثرون). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (بهم) attached to the khabar (predicate) of كان. (الواو) parenthetical. (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nāʾib fāʿil of (يوق) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (أولئك هم المفلحون) like أولئك هم الصادقون [Note: In verse (8) of this sūra.].
The clause «الذين تبوّؤا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تبوّؤا الدار ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «(ألفوا) الإيمان ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يحبّون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) [Note: The clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of تبوّؤا, if (الذين) is parsed as conjoined by the wāw to الفقراء as a conjoining of single words.].
The clause «هاجر ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «لا يجدون ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يحبّون.
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يؤثرون ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يحبّون.
The clause «كان بهم خصاصة ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "then they prefer others over themselves".
The clause «من يوق ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The clause «يوق ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «أولئك ... المفلحون» is in the position of the jussive (fī maḥall jazm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
10- (الواو) a conjunction. (الذين جاؤوا ... يقولون) like الذين تبوّؤا ... يحبّون. (من بعدهم) attached to (جاؤوا). (ربّنا) the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative. (لنا) attached to (اغفر), and likewise (لإخواننا). (بالإيمان) attached to (سبقونا). (الواو) a conjunction. (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing. (في قلوبنا) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi. (للذين) attached to (غلّا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted naʿt of (غلّا).]..
The clause «الذين جاؤوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause الذين تبوؤا.
The clause «جاؤوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) [Note: This clause may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of جاؤوا, if (الذين) is conjoined to (الذين تبوّؤا).. or have no grammatical position as an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
The clause «النداء وجوابه ...» (the vocative and its response) is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: The vocative clause may be parenthetical and the clause اغفر لنا the object of saying.].
The clause «اغفر لنا ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «سبقونا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تجعل ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative [Note: Or in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause اغفر لنا.].
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ربّنا (the second)» has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying [Note: Or resumptive, emphasising the first vocative clause.].
The clause «إنّك رؤف رحيم» has no grammatical position, being the response to the second vocative.

* Morphology:
(حاجة) see verse (68) of Sūrat Yūsuf.. What is meant by حاجة here is "envy, rage and rancour; it is a use of the entailing for the entailed, by way of metonymy (kināya), because these meanings are generally not separate from need" — from Ḥāshiyat al-Jamal.
(خصاصة) a noun for need and poverty; its origin is خصاص البيت, which are its gaps; the pattern of خصاصة is فعالة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(يوق) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion in keeping with the jussive, the lām (third radical) of the word having been deleted; its pattern is يفع, with ḍamma, then sukūn, then fatḥa..

* Rhetoric:
The device of concision (al-ījāz): in His saying, Exalted is He: وَالَّذِينَ تَبَوَّؤُا الدَّارَ وَالْإِيمانَ.
The expression is of the type of: علفتها تبنا وماء باردا (I fed her straw and [gave her] cold water), i.e. they settled in the abode and made their faith sincere.
It has been said: settling (al-tabawwuʾ) is a non-metaphorical trope (majāz mursal) for adhering, which is its concomitant meaning; it is as if it were said: they adhered to the abode and to faith. And it has been said, in explaining it: the أل in الدار is for prior reference (ʿahd), meaning the abode of emigration, and it serves as well as an annexation; and in الإيمان there is the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and the abode of faith", as if it were said: they settled in the abode of emigration and the abode of faith, the two abodes meaning Medina; the conjunction is as in your saying «رأيت الغيث والليث» (I saw the rain and the lion) when you mean Zayd.

safi-cedvel:11-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of wonder (al-istifhām al-taʿajjubī). (إلى الذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترى) in the meaning of "تنظر" (look). (لإخوانهم) attached to (يقولون). (من أهل) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of كفروا. (اللام) paving the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam). (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle. (أخرجتم) a passive past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (التاء) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (اللام) the lām of the oath. (معكم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (نخرجنّ) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of going out, i.e. "being with you"..]. (الواو) a conjunction in the two places. (لا) negative. (فيكم) attached to (نطيع), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "in humiliating you" — or "in forsaking you". (أبدا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to the negated (نطيع). (قوتلتم) like أخرجتم. (اللام) the lām of the oath, for the oath paved for by the lām omitted from (إن). (الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of the oath understood from the verb of testifying [Note: Or it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the hamza of (إنّ) was given kasra because of its presence, the original being that it have fatḥa.. The clause is then an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), or an explanation of the verb of testifying.].
The clause «لم تر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «نافقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إن أخرجتم» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نخرجنّ ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «لا نطيع ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
The clause «إن قوتلتم ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause إن أخرجتم.
The clause «ننصرنّكم ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «اللَّه يشهد ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive — or parenthetical. The clause «يشهد ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (اللَّه).
The clause «إنّهم لكاذبون ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath [Note: Or an explanatory resumption, or an explanation of the verb of testifying.].
12- (لئن أخرجوا) like لئن أخرجتم. (لا) negative. (معهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to the negated (يخرجون) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of going out, i.e. "being with you".]. [Translator's note: The note reads "with you" (معكم), repeated from verse 11; the word here is معهم, "with them".] (لئن قوتلوا لا ينصرونهم) like لئن أخرجوا لا يخرجون.. (لئن) like the first. (نصروهم) a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent) and (هم) the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (اللام) the lām of the oath. (يولّن) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was deleted because of the succession of like letters; (الواو), deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the agent, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis. (ثمّ) for conjunction. (لا) negative, and the wāw in (ينصرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «إن أخرجوا ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanation of the cause (taʿlīl) of the lying mentioned before.
The clause «لا يخرجون ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «إن قوتلوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause إن أخرجوا.
The clause «لا ينصرونهم ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «إن نصروهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause إن أخرجوا.
The clause «يولّنّ الأدبار ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «لا ينصرون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يولّنّ....
13- (اللام) the lām of the inceptive (lām al-ibtidāʾ). (رهبة) tamyīz (specification), accusative. (في صدورهم) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in أشدّ, i.e. "keeping that secret". (من اللَّه) attached to (أشدّ). The reference in (ذلك) is to their fearing the created more than the Creator. (بأنهم قوم) an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك). (لا) negative..
The clause «أنتم أشدّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا يفقهون» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.
14- (لا) negative. (جميعا) a ḥāl from the agent of يقاتلون. (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr). (في قرى) attached to (يقاتلونكم). (أو) for conjunction. (من وراء) attached to (يقاتلونكم), so it is conjoined to the first preposition phrase. (بينهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to the khabar (شديد). (جميعا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, i.e. "gathered together". (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (ذلك ... لا يعقلون) like ذلك ... لا يفقهون.
The clause «لا يقاتلونكم ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
The clause «بأسهم بينهم شديد» has no grammatical position, being another explanatory resumption.
The clause «تحسبهم جميعا» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «قلوبهم شتّى» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: Or it is a fresh resumption giving information.].
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause.
The clause «لا يعقلون» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of قوم.

* Morphology:
(13) رهبة: an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb رهب — in the passive form — its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(14) محصّنة: feminine of محصّن, a passive participle of the four-letter verb حصّن; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- The paving lām (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa)..
It is the lām that enters upon a conditional particle to announce that the response after it is built on an oath before it; hence it is called the announcing lām (al-lām al-muʾdhina), and it is also called the paving lām (al-muwaṭṭiʾa), because it paves the way for the response to the oath, i.e. prepares it for it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُوا لا يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ، وَلَئِنْ قُوتِلُوا لا يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ، وَلَئِنْ نَصَرُوهُمْ لَيُوَلُّنَّ الْأَدْبارَ. Most often it enters upon (إن). This lām may be omitted while the oath is implied before the condition, as in His saying, Exalted is He: وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ, and وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ, for this can only be a response to an oath.

safi-cedvel:15-17.t:
* I'rab:
(كمثل) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "مثلهم" (their likeness). (من قبلهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun الذين. (قريبا) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) which is the khabar [Note: Or attached to (ذاقوا).]. (الواو) a conjunction. (لهم) attached to an advanced khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب)..
The clause «(مثلهم) كمثل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ذاقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ذاقوا.
16- (كمثل) like the first [Note: The first is about the Jews and the second about the hypocrites.]. (إذ) an adverb of past time in the position of the accusative, attached to the notion of settledness which is the khabar [Note: The meaning is: the hypocrites, in their inciting the Jews, resemble Satan when he said to man: Disbelieve.]. (للإنسان) attached to (قال). (الفاء) a conjunction. (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis قال. (منك) attached to (بريء). (ربّ) a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty, accusative..
The clause «(مثلهم) كمثل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اكفر ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كفر ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال (the second)» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «إنّي بريء ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying.
The clause «إنّي أخاف ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أخاف ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
17- (الفاء) resumptive. (في النار) attached to the khabar of أنّ. (خالدين) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of settledness which is the khabar of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهما في النار..) is in the position of the nominative as the postponed noun of كان.
(الواو) resumptive, and the reference in (ذلك) is to the punishment..
The clause «كان عاقبتهما ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ذلك جزاء» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause.

safi-cedvel:18-20.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative. (الذين) a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). (الواو) a conjunction in the two places. (اللام) the lām of command. (لغد) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قدّمت). (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar (predicate) (خبير).
The vocative clause «النداء ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «تنظر نفس ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «قدّمت ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «اتّقوا ... (the second)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اتّقوا (the first).
The clause «إنّ اللَّه خبير» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
19- (الواو) a conjunction. (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing. (كالذين) attached to the khabar of تكونوا. (الفاء) a conjunction. (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun as mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is الفاسقون, the nominal clause being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]..
The clause «لا تكونوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «نسوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أنساهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause نسوا.
The clause «أولئك ... الفاسقون» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause.
20- (لا) negative. (الواو) a conjunction. (هم الفائزون) like هم الفاسقون.
The clause «لا يستوي أصحاب ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أصحاب الجنّة.. الفائزون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or explanatory of cause.

* Morphology:
(18) غد: a noun for the coming day, whether far or near; what is meant by it here is the Day of Resurrection, as if, because of its nearness, it were the next day, by way of metaphor (istiʿāra). Its pattern is فع, its lām (third radical) being deleted, since the noun of relation from it is غدويّ and غديّ.

* Rhetoric:
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, Exalted is He: وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ.
He made both النفس and الغد indefinite. As for making النفس indefinite, it is to show how few are the souls that look into what they have sent ahead for the Hereafter, as if He said: let one single soul look into that. As for making الغد indefinite, it is to magnify it and leave its matter vague, as if it were said: (the morrow) — its true nature is not known because of its extreme greatness.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (على جبل) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزلنا). (اللام) connecting the response. (خاشعا، متصدّعا) two ḥāls (circumstantials), accusative, from the absent pronoun in (رأيته). (من خشية) attached to (متصدّعا), and (من) is causal. (الواو) a conjunction. (تلك) a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), explained by the one mentioned after it.]. (للناس) attached to (نضربها)..
The clause «أنزلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «رأيته ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تلك الأمثال نضربها» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «نضربها ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (تلك).
The clause «لعلّهم يتفكّرون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتفكّرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(متصدّعا) an active participle of the five-letter verb تصدّع; its pattern is متفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:22-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الذي) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty [Note: Or a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هو.]. (لا) the lā of generic negation. (إلّا) for exception. (هو) a badal (substitute) for the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar. (عالم) a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو) [Note: Or a naʿt of the Name of Majesty.]..
The clause «هو اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «هو الرحمن ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption emphasising the content of what preceded, or for clarification.
23- (الملك) a naʿt of the Name of Majesty [Note: Or a khabar of the pronoun هو.
(2, 3) Or they are khabars of the mubtadaʾ هو.], and likewise the following attributes "2". (سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. (عمّا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (سبحان), and the returning pronoun of the relative noun is omitted.
[Translator's note: The source note above merges the texts of footnotes 1–3; markers "2" and "3" are the footnote numbers in this verse and the next.]
The clause «هو اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, being an emphasising resumption.
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحان ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
24- (الخالق) a naʿt of the Name of Majesty, and likewise the following attributes "3". (له) attached to an advanced khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الأسماء). The second (له) is attached to (يسبّح) [Note: Or the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and the pronoun, in its second position, is the object of يسبّح.. or it is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun ما, the agent.]. [Translator's note: "in its second position" renders the source's «في محلّه الثاني», which appears garbled; the intended sense seems to be "in the position of the accusative as object".] (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of ما. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — or a conjunction.
The clause «هو اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, being an emphasising resumption.
The clause «له الأسماء ...» is in the position of the nominative as another khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو.
The clause «يسبّح له ما في السموات» is in the position of the nominative as another khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو [Note: Or it is resumptive with no grammatical position.]. The clause «هو العزيز ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: Or it is conjoined to the clause يسبّح.].

* Morphology:
(23) القدّوس: an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) from (قدس), meaning "to be pure"; its pattern is فعّول, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn with ḍamma.
(السلام) an adjective resembling the active participle from (سلم), i.e. "possessor of soundness"; its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(24) المصوّر: an active participle of the four-letter verb (صوّر); its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب}: «مِنْ» may be for clarification, so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e., "I mean from the People of the Book". The second: it is a ḥāl from «الذين كفروا».
His saying: {مِن دِيَارِهِمْ}: attached to «أَخْرَجَ»; its meaning is the beginning of the limit. Annexing the homes to them is sound because they built them.
His saying: {لأَوَّلِ الحشر}: this lām is attached to «أَخْرَجَ» and is the lām of timing, as in His saying {لِدُلُوكِ الشمس} [al-Isrāʾ: 78], i.e., at the first gathering. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the lām in His saying the Exalted {ياليتني قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي} [al-Fajr: 24] and in your saying 'I came for such-and-such a time'." I say: the discussion of this lām will come in al-Fajr, God willing.
His saying: {مَّانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُم}: two views. One: «حصونُهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «مانِعَتُهم» a fronted khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «أنهم». It is not to be said: why not say «مانِعَتُهم» is the mubtadaʾ because it is definite, and «حصونُهم» its khabar? There is no need for fronting or postponing, because the intention is to report about the fortresses, and because the annexation is not a true one (ghayr maḥḍa), so it is indefinite. The second: «مانِعَتُهم» is the khabar of «أنهم» and «حصونُهم» is the agent through it, like "inna Zaydan qāʾimun abūhu" and "inna ʿAmran qāʾimatun jāriyatuhu". The Shaykh preferred it, because in the like of "qāʾimun Zaydun", whether it be a fronted khabar and postponed mubtadaʾ, there is disagreement, and the Kufans forbid it; so the place of agreement is preferable.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what difference is there between your saying 'and they thought that their fortresses would protect them', or 'protectors of them', and the arrangement in which it came? I say: in fronting the khabar before the mubtadaʾ there is an indication of the extreme of their confidence in the fortresses' strength and in their protecting them, and in making their pronoun the noun of «أنَّ» and predicating the clause of it there is an indication of their belief about themselves that they were in might and defence such that they cared nothing for anyone who might confront them; and that is not in your saying 'their fortresses protect them'." End of quotation. What he mentioned works only on the first i'rab, and it has already been mentioned that it is the weaker. Here "thinking" is made to operate on the doubled «أنَّ», though the rule is that nothing operates on it or on its lightened form except a verb of knowledge and certainty; so [thinking] is treated like certainty because of its strength and because it stands in the position of knowledge.
His saying: {يُخْرِبُونَ}: it may be resumptive, to report it, and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قلوبِهم», though not likely. Abū ʿAmr read «يُخَرِّبون» doubled and the rest lightened; they have one meaning, because Abū ʿAmr made kharraba transitive by doubling and they by the hamza. From Abū ʿAmr it is reported that he distinguished them with another meaning, saying: "kharraba with doubling: he demolished and spoiled; and akhraba with hamza: he left the place in ruins and went away from it." Al-Hudhalī preferred Abū ʿAmr's reading for the sake of intensification. «يُخْرِبون» may also be an explication of the terror, so it too has no position.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {الجلاء}: the majority [read it] with the lengthened form, which is expulsion: ajlaytu al-qawma ijlāʾan, and jalā he went into exile, jalāʾan. Al-Māwardī said: "Al-jalāʾ is more specific than leaving, because it is said only of a group, while expulsion applies to a group or one." Another said: the difference between them is that jalāʾ is with family and children, unlike expulsion, which does not require that.
Al-Ḥasan and ʿAlī, sons of Ṣāliḥ, read «الجَلا» with an alif only. Ṭalḥa [read it] with hamza without alif, like «al-naba'». Ṭalḥa read «ومَنْ يُشاقِقْ» with unassimilated doubling, as is agreed upon in al-Anfāl.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {مَا قَطَعْتُمْ}: «ما» is conditional, in the position of the accusative through «قَطَعْتم», and «مِن لينةٍ» is a clarification of it. «فبإِذنِ اللهِ» is the apodosis of the condition. An omission is necessary, i.e., "its cutting is by Allah's permission", so «بإذنِ الله» is the khabar of that mubtadaʾ. There is much disagreement about the līna. It is said: it is the palm tree in general, and he recited:
4244 - As if my saddle-frame upon her were a bird's nest ... on a long-stemmed palm whose sides sway
and another said:
4245 - Wings spread, settled above a līna ... the dew of its night glistening on its feathers
It is also said: it is the palm tree that is not an ʿajwa. It is also said: that which is neither ʿajwa nor barniyya. It is also said: the noble palm. It is also said: a palm whose dates are a "colour" (lawn), a kind of date; Sufyān said: it is intensely yellow, translucent to the stone. It is also said: it is the ʿajwa. It is also said: it is the saplings (fusilān), and he recited:
4246 - They planted a līna by a flowing stream ... then the palms were enclosed with thickets
and another said:
4247 - The loved ones have shunned me when they sang ... of parting from the loved ones, from atop a līna
It is also said: it is the tree's branches, for their softness.
There are two views on the ʿayn of «لِينة». One: it is a wāw, because it is from lawn (colour), and it was turned into yāʾ because of its quiescence and the kasra before it, like dīma and qīma. The second: it is a yāʾ, because it is from līn (softness). The plural of līna is līn, because it is of the type of collective noun like tamra and tamr. It has also been broken as «līyān», which is irregular, because breaking what is distinguished by the feminine tāʾ is irregular, like ruṭaba, ruṭab and arṭāb. He recited:
4248 - And a neck like the crushing of the līyān ... which the misguided one set afire with flames
The pronoun in «تَرَكْتموها» returns to the sense of «ما». ʿAbd Allāh, al-Aʿmash and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «قُوَّماً» on the pattern of ḍurrab, plural of qāʾim, observing the sense of «ما», which is plural. «قائماً» has also been read, singular masculine. «أُصُلِها» has also been read without wāw. There are two views: one, that it is the plural of aṣl, like rahn and ruhun. The second, that he dropped the wāw as heavy.
His saying: {وَلِيُخْزِيَ}: the lām is attached to an omitted element, i.e., "and He permitted cutting it so that He may disgrace", or "so that He may gladden the believers and strengthen them, and so that He may disgrace".

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {فَمَآ أَوْجَفْتُمْ}: the fāʾ is the apodosis of the condition, or redundant, on the basis that it is a relative noun containing the sense of a condition. «ما» is negative. Al-ījāf is making a camel go at a quick pace; one says wajafa the camel, yajifu, wajfan, wajīfan and wajafānan. I made it do so: awjaftuhu ījāfan. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
4249 - A swift one, whom weariness from his trotting had folded up
and Nuṣayb said:
4250 - How many a riding party whose trotting I have crossed ... to you, and but for you the party would not have trotted
His saying: {مِنْ خَيْلٍ}: «مِنْ» is redundant, i.e., "horses". Al-rikāb are the camels.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {مَّآ أَفَآءَ الله}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He did not insert a conjunction before this clause because it is an explanation of the first, so it is not foreign to it."
His saying: {يَكُونَ دُولَةً}: Hishām read «تكون» with the tāʾ and, [with it,] «دُوْلةٌ» nominative only; the rest [read] with the yāʾ and put «دُوْلَةً» in the accusative. As for the nominative, it is on the basis that it is the complete «كان». The masculine and feminine are clear since the feminine is figurative. As for the accusative, it is on the basis that it is the incomplete kāna; its noun is a pronoun returning to the fayʾ, and the masculine is necessary because of the masculine nominative; and «دُولة» is its khabar. It is also said that it returns to «ما», taking its wording into account. The majority read «دُوْلة» with ḍamma on the dāl; ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and al-Sulamī [read it] with fatḥa. It is said: they are equivalent, being what turns (yadūlu) for a person, i.e., revolves, of effort, hardship and victory. The experts among the Basrans, and al-Kisāʾī, said: al-dawla with fatḥa is from al-mulk with ḍamma on the mīm, and with ḍamma from al-milk with kasra; or with ḍamma in wealth and with fatḥa in victory. The reading transmitted from ʿAlī and al-Sulamī refutes this, since victory is certainly not intended here. «كيلا» is a reason for His saying «فللَّهِ وللرسول», i.e., its settling for such-and-such is for this reason.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لِلْفُقَرَآءِ}: three views. One: it is a badal from «لذي القُرْبى»; Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī said it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is said that it is a badal from «لذي القُربى» and what follows it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "A badal from His saying «ولذي القُربى» and what is conjoined to it. What prevented substituting from «لله وللرسول» and what is conjoined to them, although the meaning is 'to the Messenger of Allah', is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic excluded His Messenger from the poor in His saying {وَيَنصُرُونَ الله وَرَسُولَهُ}, and that He the Exalted exalts His Messenger above being named poor, and that substituting according to the apparent wording departs from what is obligatory in glorifying Allah the Mighty and Majestic." He means: if it were said that it is a badal from «لله» and what follows it, what he mentioned would follow: that the badal, according to the apparent wording, would be from the Majestic Name, so one would say that «للفقراء» is a badal from «لله» and from «رسوله», which is ugly in wording, even if the meaning is contrary to this apparent sense, as he said: its meaning is "to the Messenger of Allah", and Allah the Mighty and Majestic is mentioned only for magnification, otherwise Allah the Exalted is free of need of the fayʾ and other things. He made it a badal from «لذي القُرْبى» only because he is a Ḥanafī, and the Ḥanafīs make poverty a condition for giving the relatives share from the fayʾ.
The second: it is a clarification of His saying {والمساكين وابن السبيل}, and the genitive lām was repeated, since the first was genitive by the lām, to make clear that the badal is from it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it, and it is a very unsettled expression. The third: «للفقراء» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "but the fayʾ is for the poor". It is also said: its implied form is "but it is for the poor".
